articles.title_orig: The political economy of China’s e-CNY reform
articles.title_zh: The political economy of China’s e-CNY reform
articles.content_orig:
Peer reviewed analysis from world leading experts
China’s 2026 e‑CNY reform turns eligible digital yuan balances into interest‑bearing commercial bank deposits, giving banks stronger incentives to promote adoption of the digital currency. Restrictions on cryptocurrency and stablecoins reflect Beijing’s preference for keeping digital currency within the existing monetary and regulatory system. By increasing the commercial usefulness and operational convenience of the digital yuan, the People’s Bank of China may be able to drive both domestic and international adoption of both the currency and the system through which it circulates.
On 1 January 2026, the People’s Bank of China (PBoC) changed the monetary framework governing the digital yuan (e-CNY), a digital form of the renminbi designed for use in payments, making it the world’s first interest-bearing central bank digital currency. The reform shifts commercial banks from being largely passive distributors of central bank digital money to institutions with a direct commercial stake in expanding use of the e-CNY.
From the beginning of its pilot programs in 2019, the e-CNY was classified as M0, a direct central bank liability comparable to physical banknotes . Commercial banks were required to distribute and support the e-CNY despite limited opportunities to earn revenue from it, with one prominent commentator identifying weak commercial incentives as a limitation of the original model. Because e-CNY balances were treated as digital cash rather than deposits, they did not contribute to banks’ deposit bases and could potentially compete with existing products and services.
Under the new framework, eligible e-CNY balances held through commercial banks are classified as M1, the measure of the money supply that includes cash and demand deposits. The reform shifts these balances away from the logic of ‘outside money’ issued directly by the central bank and towards ‘inside money’ created and managed within the commercial banking system. Eligible e-CNY balances can now earn interest, receive deposit insurance protection, and enter commercial banks’ balance sheets, reserve requirement calculations and asset-liability management. Promoting the e-CNY can become part of ordinary banking business rather than an administrative obligation which sits alongside it.
The broader lesson of this reform is that financial infrastructure does not automatically translate into adoption. State direction can create the channels for a currency to circulate, but uptake depends on whether the institutions expected to carry out that policy have incentives to do so.
China already has one of the world’s most developed mobile payment ecosystems, dominated by Alipay and WeChat Pay , which benefit from powerful network effects and are deeply embedded in everyday commercial life. Alipay users can move idle balances into yield-generating products such as Yu’e Bao. The initial e-CNY design offered most consumers few obvious advantages over services they were already using.
Allowing eligible balances to earn interest removes one disadvantage. But the larger effect may come from changing the behaviour of banks. If banks have a commercial interest in expanding e-CNY deposits, they have more reason to integrate the currency into payment services, customer relationships and other areas of financial activity.
The number of authorised e-CNY operating institutions has expanded rapidly throughout 2026. Twelve additional banks were admitted in April and another eight in August, bringing the total number of operators to 30 . Newer participants include joint-stock commercial banks and city commercial banks, extending the system beyond the large state-owned banks that dominated the earlier phase.
The reform illustrates a broader feature of the e-CNY’s evolving political economy. Rather than relying on administrative direction alone, the PBoC is redesigning the institutional framework so that commercial incentives work in support of the state’s objective to expand the digital yuan.
The same logic is also becoming visible in the e-CNY’s cross-border development. In June 2026, China’s e-CNY International Operations Center signed agreements with 26 financial institutions as the first direct participants in the Cross-Border e-CNY Transfer Services (CBETS) program. The initial group included institutions in Hong Kong, Macau, Singapore, Laos, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Brazil.
This does not mean that the digital yuan is about to transform the international monetary system. Its importance lies more in the way domestic reform and cross-border infrastructure are beginning to reinforce one another . Treating eligible e-CNY balances more like commercial bank deposits makes them easier to integrate into banking operations, while systems such as CBETS give banks additional reasons to develop cross-border services around them. Yet as with renminbi internationalisation more broadly, international use will not simply depend on the existence of infrastructure, but on whether banks, firms and trading partners find the currency commercially useful and operationally convenient.
The e-CNY also forms part of a broader shift in China’s approach to digital finance. In February 2026, Chinese regulators reinforced restrictions on crypto assets and explicitly prohibited the unauthorised issuance of offshore renminbi-pegged stablecoins, while continuing to privilege the e-CNY as the principal vehicle for digitalising sovereign money. This reflects Beijing’s preference for keeping digital currency within the existing monetary and regulatory system, rather than allowing privately issued dollar-denominated stablecoins to dominate digital finance in China .
Yet better payment infrastructure does not remove the main constraints on wider international use of the renminbi. Capital controls, limited convertibility and the continued depth and liquidity of dollar-denominated financial markets remain substantial barriers, as do the commercial routines and network effects that continue to favour established currencies in trade and finance.
Having changed the relationship between the central bank, commercial banks and the digital yuan, the 2026 redesign raises a more fundamental question about what the e-CNY is becoming. As eligible balances increasingly resemble conventional bank deposits, the PBoC appears to be shifting from creating a distinctive form of digital cash towards embedding the e-CNY within a state-governed banking and payments infrastructure. The digital yuan’s defining feature may therefore lie primarily in the centrally designed system through which it circulates — one that can connect banks, payments and cross-border transactions.
Monique Taylor is Lecturer and Docent in World Politics at the University of Helsinki.

articles.title_orig: China helps dismantle major meth trafficking network in Southeast Asia
articles.title_zh: China helps dismantle major meth trafficking network in Southeast Asia
articles.content_orig:
Joint operation with Indonesia and Malaysia shuts down what is believed to be Indonesia’s largest methamphetamine laboratory
China has broken up a major transnational drug trafficking network in cooperation with Indonesia and Malaysia, seizing around 1.2 tonnes of liquid methamphetamine, China’s Ministry of Public Security said on Friday.
The operation was carried out on October 21 by Indonesia’s National Narcotics Agency (BNN), which raided and shut down a large-scale drug processing and purification facility in Aceh, Indonesia, and arrested 11 people, with help from China’s National Narcotics Control Commission (NNCC) and Malaysia’s National Anti-Drugs Agency, the ministry said.
The methamphetamine factory, housed in two shops, is believed to be the largest of its kind in Indonesia. Washing machines used to process methamphetamine, liquefied petroleum gas cylinders and other equipment and materials were also found at the site, according to local media reports.

articles.title_orig: As I See It | The flaw in Australia’s ‘China threat’ thesis
articles.title_zh: As I See It | The flaw in Australia’s ‘China threat’ thesis
articles.content_orig:
Instead of adopting Washington’s security priorities, Canberra should leverage superpower rivalry to its own advantage, argues policy veteran John Edwards
Australia’s preparations for a possible conflict with China reflect “a relatively superficial understanding”, argues prominent economist John Edwards. Europe, Canada, Indonesia, Malaysia and India, he notes, are not preparing for such a conflict. Why should Australia?
Instead, he sees US-China rivalry as a potential advantage. Sitting between a security partner in Washington and a major economic partner in Beijing can underpin Australian prosperity for 25 years – provided Canberra does not pick sides.

articles.title_orig: Tusk-Nawrocki battle escalates as chief judge is ousted from Poland’s top court
articles.title_zh: Tusk-Nawrocki battle escalates as chief judge is ousted from Poland’s top court
articles.content_orig:
Poland’s constitutional court descended into turmoil Friday evening as judges barred from hearing cases moved to oust the institution’s nationalist-linked leadership, sparking accusations of a coup and tense protests.
Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, a judge with the court, ordered its president Bogdan Święczkowski and his deputy to be suspended for a month and announced she was taking charge . Święczkowski rejected her authority , accusing those involved of a “coup d’état,” while his deputy was turned away at the building’s gates.
The showdown marks an escalation in Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s struggle to undo the judicial overhaul carried out by the nationalist Law and Justice (PiS) former government. During its eight years in power, PiS filled the Constitutional Tribunal with its appointees, including Święczkowski and his deputy, placing it at the heart of Poland’s confrontation with Brussels over the rule of law.
Outside the tribunal, protesters clashed with police , who said objects had been thrown at officers and three people detained after climbing over the court’s fence. Police said they had deployed to maintain security following warnings of threats to judges and staff, but had not entered the building.
PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński took part in the protest and tried to force his way into the court building. He accused Tusk of staging a “coup” against the court and turning Poland into a “police state,” and demanded presidential intervention.
President Karol Nawrocki, a PiS ally and rival of Tusk, interrupted his official trip to Senegal, declaring , “At a moment like this, the president must be in Poland.”
Tusk was defiant. “Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” he wrote on X . “After years of PiS lawlessness, it’s a difficult, sometimes painful process that requires decisive action. There is no other way.”
The tribunal, which can strike down legislation, helped impose a near-total abortion ban under PiS and challenged the supremacy of EU law . Last December, the EU’s top court ruled that it failed to meet European standards of judicial independence.
But efforts to change the court’s makeup have met resistance. Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges elected by Tusk’s parliamentary majority. They took their oaths in parliament instead, but Święczkowski barred them from hearing cases.
Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek blamed the turmoil on Święczkowski, who he accused of turning the institution into his “private fiefdom” and preventing newly elected judges from doing their jobs.
“And now the judges have spoken,” Żurek told POLITICO.
Żurek, who also serves as Poland’s prosecutor general, said he submitted five requests to lift the immunity of Święczkowski and his deputy, backed by 50 volumes of case files. He defended Korwin-Piotrowska’s move as a decision by a legally appointed judge, insisting that the government had nothing to do with it.

articles.title_orig: Iran says 4 tankers strike mines and catch fire in Strait of Hormuz, and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Iran says 4 tankers strike mines and catch fire in Strait of Hormuz, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
Follow updates on the war in the Middle East for Friday, Oct. 30, here . See earlier developments below.
The U.S. Department of Defense has added two more service member deaths to its official account of casualties since the war with Iran started more than eight months ago, bringing the overall death toll to 23.
Both of the newly noted deaths on the Defense Casualty Analysis System portal were noncombat related. In total the DCAS portal says 11 service members have been killed by enemy fire during the war, and 12 others have died under circumstances deemed nonhostile, which includes accidents and sickness.
Both of the service members recently added as nonhostile deaths were airmen, including one who died of an illness and the another from unspecified causes that remain under investigation, The Washington Post quoted the Air Force as saying.
The two deaths added to the DCAS system are listed under Overseas Operations , which includes deaths recorded by the Pentagon after it stopped using the name Operation Epic Fury for the offensive against Iran in May, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared the operation over.
The Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Mecca region that had been fired by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels.
"A drone launched by the terrorist Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed in the Mecca region," the coalition wrote in a post on X.
The Houthis denied any attempt to strike Saudi Arabia on Friday, the Reuters news agency reports.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on social media that the group hadn't conducted any operations aimed at Saudi territory, adding that the Houthis only target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.
Explosions rocked the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh on Thursday hours after the Iran-backed Houthis reported deadly strikes earlier in the day on residential areas of western Yemen that the Houthis said killed at least 12 people.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said on Thursday it had downed two ballistic missiles launched by the group towards Riyadh, soon after Agence France-Presse correspondents heard fresh explosions in the capital.
"Air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said on X.
Earlier, AFP correspondents in Riyadh had heard at least eight explosions as authorities warned the city was "under a hostile aerial threat" in a phone alert.
Saudi civil defense had issued warnings for "potential danger" in Riyadh, Kharj and the southern city of Najran that were lifted shortly afterward.
The Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on the Riyadh airport that forced its shuttering for two weeks as flagship events were canceled, threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
The Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni government have exchanged daily attacks since a yearslong truce fell apart over the summer.
A tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz around 7:30 p.m. local time (noon Eastern time), according to the U.K. Marine Trade Operations Centre .
The ship was exiting the strait along the southern route, promoted by the U.S., when it came under fire.
"There are no reported injuries to the crew or environmental impact … at this time," the UKMTO said.
While it wasn't clear who fired the projectile, Iran has taken credit for several ships hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday and has been targeting ships along the southern route at an increased rate.
Iran has not yet responded to a letter sent by Vice President JD Vance to the secretary of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, according to the semi-official Tasnim News agency, which is closely affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Tasnim said in a Thursday post on its official Telegram social media account that Tehran was not prepared to drop any of its core conditions for a ceasefire, which include lifting the American blockade of Iran's ports, easing sanctions and giving Iran access to its frozen financial assets held abroad, among other things.
Multiple news outlets have reported that Vance's letter to Rezaei was an attempt to restart peace negotiations, but President Trump said Wednesday that it was a focused outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.
Iran's navy said a tanker it described as violating maritime restrictions was damaged and caught fire after striking sea mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the vessel unable to continue sailing.
In a statement, the navy said the incident occurred before noon on Thursday as the tanker was sailing through an area designated as prohibited and unsafe by Iran
The U.S. has encouraged shippers to use a shipping route in the south of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has insisted vessels can only use northern routes it has authorized.
The navy's statement warned that the Strait of Hormuz was closed "to violating vessels that, without coordination and relying on the lies of the U.S. president, intend to pass through prohibited and unsafe areas."
"These uncoordinated transits through high-risk areas have exposed and will continue to expose vessels and their crews to serious dangers," it added.
Qatar has categorically denied allegations of interfering in Israel's elections or funding efforts to influence their outcome, accusing Israeli politicians and media figures of launching a disinformation campaign to drag the small Persian Gulf state into domestic Israeli political disputes.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Majid al-Ansari said in a statement that Qatar would not be used as a scapegoat for Israeli politicians' failures, insisting that Doha had no involvement in Israel's political competition and would continue its mediation efforts between Iran and the U.S., as well as wider diplomatic engagement and support for the Palestinian people.
His comments come after Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that Tuesday's national elections were "stolen by Arab parties" and claimed foreign interference in the vote.
Israel's Shin Bet internal security service is investigating possible Qatari and Turkish funding used in an effort to influence the election outcome, according to reports by the Jerusalem Post and Israel's Channel 13.
"These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure," al-Ansari said. "The repeated invocation of Qatar in Israeli electoral rhetoric reveals an excessive obsession with our country among certain Israeli political and media figures."
Iran's navy has carried out more than 20 operations against U.S. warships and approximately 300 operations targeting American interests in various locations during the war, Iranian Army Navy Coordinating Deputy Rear Admiral Jalil Moghadam said in an interview published Thursday by the official state-run news agency IRNA .
Moghadam claimed the operations involved missiles and drones and said Iran's navy remains operational despite repeated claims by President Trump and other U.S. officials saying it has been destroyed.
"If the Iranian Navy has been destroyed, why have these forces not come closer than 500 or 600 kilometers to the Strait of Hormuz, or closer than 300 kilometers to our maritime borders? There is a force standing in their way, and that force must be the Navy," he said.
Moghadam did not offer any evidence to substantiate his claims.
IRGC spokesperson Brig. Gen. Abolfazl Mohebi challenged U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) to provide independent evidence for its claims of mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz.
"Prove your claim of mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz with independent evidence, not a statement!" demanded Mohebi in a post on X , adding that "the reality of the Strait of Hormuz is determined in the skies, on land and at sea — not on social media or in Am

articles.title_orig: China’s Fourth Aircraft Carrier Could Arrive as Soon as Next Year
articles.title_zh: China’s Fourth Aircraft Carrier Could Arrive as Soon as Next Year
articles.content_orig:
By ELINA SHIRAZI, US SENIOR POLITICAL REPORTER
Published: 13:43 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 18:12 EDT, 30 October 2026
A dramatic surge in military tension has taken center stage as President Trump ordered a third US aircraft carrier to the Middle East – all while making cryptic claims that the standoff will soon reach its conclusion.
US Central Command confirmed that bringing three aircraft carrier strike groups into the Middle East represents the largest US naval surge in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq .
Trump voiced confidence today that the conflict would dissipate, though he provided no specific timeline or strategy for how that outcome would be secured.
'It's going to get wrapped up soon,' Trump stated during an interview with a Kansas City radio station. 'We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon.'
The remarks comes as questions surrounding Trump's domestic campaign itinerary arise, with the President rescheduling several canceled rallies over the weekend.
Vice President JD Vance also canceled a scheduled Friday press briefing in St. Cloud, Minnesota , focused on the administration's 'War on Fraud.'
Officials have not provided a reason for the cancellation.
Recent reports suggest the administration is laying the groundwork for a fresh wave of aggressive military strikes if Iranian leaders refuse to sign an agreement.
The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln is pictured
During campaign appearances, he has argued that hostilities will wrap up shortly following the midterms, provided the GOP retains control of Congress
Despite initiating the war in February expecting a rapid surrender from Iran's weakened regime, Trump has continuously maintained that the conflict will draw to a close, even while combat intensifies and global economic damage continues to mount.
This has led to voter dissatisfaction across both parties ahead of the midterm elections.
During campaign appearances, he has argued that hostilities will wrap up shortly following the midterms, provided the GOP retains control of Congress.
Two US officials report that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit are scheduled to arrive in the Middle East by late November.
Upon arrival, the Roosevelt will operate alongside the USS George H.W. Bush, which deployed in April, and the USS George Washington, which arrived in August as a replacement for the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Meanwhile, the nation's highest–ranking Middle East commander has reportedly briefed Trump on potential strike scenarios regarding Iran.
Admiral Brad Cooper visited the White House on Thursday with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the Wall Street Journal reports.
As Trump evaluates strategy options for resuming military action against Iran, the discussion with cabinet officials included potential plans for maintaining the ongoing regional blockade.
Following a high-level White House meeting involving military leadership and Vice President Vance, Hegseth removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia from his role as top strategist for the Joint Chiefs.
Sylvia's removal comes amid allegations that he leaked classified intelligence regarding the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

articles.title_orig: King visits Guyanese slave rebellion site on Caribbean tour
articles.title_zh: King visits Guyanese slave rebellion site on Caribbean tour
articles.content_orig:
The King has made a poignant visit to the site where a Guyanese slave rebellion was violently resisted by British authorities, making the stop during his tour of the Caribbean.
He visited Independence Park in Georgetown to remember the Demerera Slave Rebellion of 1823, which saw an uprising by thousands of enslaved people.
Accompanied by Guyana's Culture Minister, Steven Jacobs, he was told how hundreds of slaves were killed by colonial leaders during the rebellion and many of those who survived were executed close to where the King stood.
Above the King was a sign that he took time to read.
"This ground was used as a public execution site," it said, "where enslaved persons...were condemned to death and hung."
The moment of reflection was what Buckingham Palace had described as the King "not shying away from the UK's colonial legacy" and described today as a chance for the King to reflect on Guyana's history of slavery and resistance.
In 2022, Charles described how he was on a personal journey of discovery and was continuing to "deepen my own understanding of slavery's enduring impact", in a speech at the opening of a Commonwealth summit hosted by Rwanda .
Independence Park, which is now a sports ground, drew a crowd of dozens of schoolchildren. The King stopped to talk to many of them asking them about their homework, their holidays and if they'd had a day off school.
Outside one of the King's engagements later in the day, a small but noisy group of protesters gathered.
Many held placards saying "no apology will return what was stolen, reparations now" and "justice must not depend on wealth status and connections".
"This great wealth was built on the backs of slavery," said protester, Guyanese politician, Terrence Campbell.
"I do not want the British public to think that by me saying reparations can take various forms, it means that they do not have responsibility for reparations. They do, because the United Kingdom benefited tremendously from slavery."
The King will not be apologising for the UK involvement in the slave trade during the visit, nor will he offer reparations - compensation from those countries who benefited from the slave trade - in line with the position of the UK government.
This tour has seen a number of demonstrations so far but none have seriously disrupted the King's programme.
Royal tours often include cultural exchanges and the King's trip to Guyana saw an unusual mix up of musical styles.
On the bandstand of Promenade Gardens in Georgetown, the bagpipes of the National Piping Centre could be heard alongside traditional Guyanese drummers in a collaboration of musical styles.
Seven pipers from the National Piping Centre have been touring Guyana over the past week to learn more about the Guyanese musical traditions.
As part of his visit on Friday, the King also shared a moment with a veterans from Guyana who fought for Britain in the Second World War during an event at the Commonwealth War Graves in the capital Georgetown.
King Charles met Donald Grant, 99, who will celebrate his 100th birthday next week on November 3.
He also spoke to James Samuel, 100, who is in a wheelchair, with the the King hearing how aged 19 he enlisted in the British Guiana Volunteer Force in 1943.
"What a great pleasure it is to see you on this occasion," the King told him.
The King was waved off at the end of his state visit by Britain's High Commissioner to Guyana, Joseph Fisher, Guyana's Prime Minister Mark Phillips and a number of other dignitaries.
His departure had a small ceremonial element with the Guyana Defence Force providing a guard of honour at Cheddi Jagan International Airport.

articles.title_orig: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
articles.title_zh: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
articles.content_orig:
As OpenAI’s buying spree squeezes the world’s supply of RAM, its CEO explains why he needs so much.﻿
As OpenAI’s buying spree squeezes the world’s supply of RAM, its CEO explains why he needs so much.﻿
Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage , OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it’s “terrible” to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers. During his appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he also commented on AI’s impact on math , Altman said:
“A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open-source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.
But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.
You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow everyone’s— many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”
Whether Altman meant your gaming PC or developers working with something like the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box or the new touchscreen MacBook Pro , the outcome is the same. Right now, memory companies Samsung and SK Hynix have long term deals with cloud service operators and projects like OpenAI’s Stargate that have reserved much of the world’s RAM output over the next few years. And the billions they’re willing to lay out for chips is why the laptops, phones, and other tech you use are getting more expensive right now.

articles.title_orig: Italy’s PM deploys troops as nation faces widespread strikes and port blockades
articles.title_zh: Italy’s PM deploys troops as nation faces widespread strikes and port blockades
articles.content_orig:
ROME — Tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Rome, Milan and other Italian cities Friday as part of nationwide demonstrations against the cost of living and high military spending.
After several weeks of violent protests in Italy and throughout Europe , more widespread disruption is expected after the Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) and other trade unions called on workers in both the public and private sectors to strike and protest.
The demonstrations in Italy appear to have been partly inspired by those in France , where some of the worst rioting in decades erupted in cities across the country after student protests about the state of education in the country evolved into wider actions about the cost of living and social security.
Elsewhere in Europe, a huge encampment of tents has occupied a square in Madrid since late last month, and thousands of people in Portugal have taken to the streets in the city of Lisbon. Tear gas and water cannons were also used on black-clad protesters in Brussels.
In Rome, many waved communist and Palestinian flags, as well as signs against the Iran war. Some let off pink smoke bombs. There was a jovial mood among the demonstrators as they lined up before the march, as has often been the case early on at previous protests, only for violence to break out later.
Protesters storm the Colosseum in Rome
Giovanna Di Matteo, a member of the left-wing Potere al Popolo! party, said she was protesting against the government that “did nothing for the people of this country.”
The government had spent money on the military “while they cut on welfare, they cut on services and people cannot reach the end of the month,” she said. “They have no money for their houses, they have no money for gasoline and everything.”
Luca, a 20-year-old medical student said the protesters felt they were “still not being heard, that everything is still the same,” and the government didn’t “care about our voice, about our voices, and about the future of this nation that is our nation.”
“We have been completely screwed by the fact that the wages do not keep up on inflation and the wages in general do not keep up with the cost of living,” added Luca, asked to have his last name withheld out of fear of repercussions from law enforcement.
Major demonstrations also took place in other cities and towns across Italy.
They came after a number of protests in recent weeks have turned violent. Groups of masked protesters looted stores in Milan and elsewhere and threw projectiles at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons earlier this month.
Italian police were out in force again Friday with riot brigades, drones and helicopters visible in the skies above the Rome protest.
Their presence was heavy after protesters stormed Rome’s historic Colosseum on Saturday, while in the south, farmers and truckers have blockaded highways and ports to protest high fuel prices which have risen since the United States and Israel launched the war against Iran.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni , who has made law and order a key tenet of her administration, said she had “great respect” for peaceful protesters on X earlier this month.
But her right-wing government has since introduced tougher penalties for rioters, including financial liability for parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.
“There is nothing revolutionary about vandalizing and stealing. Vandalism and theft are not protest, they are criminality,” Meloni said on social media after unveiling the legislation.
The government also said it would deploy 500 army troops alongside the police in Milan until the end of the year.
NBC News Chief Foreign Correspondent
Sara Monetta is a multimedia producer based in London.

articles.title_orig: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.title_zh: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.content_orig:
The United States has scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
The move exposes deep rifts at the heart of the Group of 20 (G20), whose foreign ministers are meeting in the southern city of Atlanta in the United States for talks overshadowed by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
“There will be no family photo featuring our European partners together with Mr Lavrov,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, according to the dpa news agency.
Lavrov, who remains under Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, arrived in Atlanta ahead of the talks, Russian state media reported. Moscow said on Thursday that he would use his speech to argue against international sanctions. Ukraine was not invited, the Abu Dhabi-based newspaper The National reported.
A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Russia’s presence at the G20 “in no way legitimises its actions”.
The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas pledged on Thursday to urge G20 partners to strengthen support for Ukraine and pursue accountability through a special tribunal and claims commission, after a Russian strike on a Ukrainian railway station killed at least 14 people earlier that day.
The meeting also comes weeks after US President Donald Trump issued sanctions waivers allowing Russia to export diesel to ease fuel prices before the November 3 midterm elections.
Opening the talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged members to cooperate on economic and geopolitical crises threatening global trade, energy and food supplies, and freedom of navigation, dpa reported. Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz after US-Israeli strikes began in late February, and global energy prices have risen sharply since.
“Both maritime and food security drive economic security,” Rubio wrote on X.
No joint statement is expected. A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Washington will instead publish a chair’s summary it has drafted. The source added: “The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement.”
No government has said whether Rubio and Lavrov will hold a formal bilateral meeting.
China sent Executive Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu in place of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, according to a delegation list released by the Department of State. South Africa, a founding G20 member, has been excluded by Washington, and the African Union is represented by Burundi’s Edouard Bizimana.
The Atlanta talks are the last ministerial meeting of the US G20 presidency before leaders meet in Miami on December 14 and 15.

Polish president Karol Nawrocki turned back his plane en route to Senegal on Friday as the country’s top court was thrown into chaos after its president was suspended.
Police and protesters clashed outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after the government suspended its two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them. Reports suggest riot police were deployed on Friday evening as demonstrators supporting the Law and Order (PiS) party, who oppose the government, threw objects at officers.
"At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland . I am cutting short my flight to Senegal. I am returning," Mr Nawrocki, who is backed by the PiS, said on X.
The tribunal ⁠said on its website that the court's president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, ​had ⁠been suspended on Friday.
A ‌long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralysed the institution.
Earlier this year, Mr Nawrocki, an ally of ‌Poland's former nationalist government of the Law ‌and Justice or PiS party, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski, who was a deputy ⁠justice minister under PiS, declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties.
Restoring the rule of law is the government's duty, prime minister Donald Tusk said on X later on Friday.
“Restoring the rule of law is our obligation,” prime minister Tusk wrote on X on Friday evening. “After years of lawlessness under PiS this is a difficult process, sometimes painful and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.”
Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek told ‌reporters he has requested the ⁠lifting of the immunities of Swieczkowski and his deputy ⁠for failing to fulfill their duties by preventing judges from performing their ‌work.
PiS politicians, ​including leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski, said Tusk's ‌government was carrying out a ​coup on the tribunal.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash burn fears spark tech selloff
articles.title_zh: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash burn fears spark tech selloff
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
US stocks plunged in the final trading day of the month as earnings from Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) this week rekindled concerns about the amount of money Big Tech is spending on its AI ambitions.
The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 2.8% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1.2%, or over 650 points, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 2%.
For the month, the Dow gained 1.5%, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 gave up gains, falling 5.2% and 1.2%, respectively. October marked the worst month for the Nasdaq since March 2025.
Stocks fell for the second day in a row after Amazon and Alphabet posted rare earnings misses , renewing concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Amazon shares fell 2%, while Alphabet continued to erase market value after its stock suffered its worst day in over 20 years.
Intel ( INTC ) also suffered a brutal reaction to its earnings report, dropping 29% in premarket trading after the company's Q4 outlook came up short.
One bright spot in the market was ExxonMobil ( XOM ) and Chevron ( CVX ), whose stocks briefly touched record highs after the oil majors reported that their earnings were boosted as refining margins widened amid the war in the Middle East. Pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca ( AZN ) also reported an earnings beat before the opening bell.
While earnings remain in focus, oil prices rebounded higher, putting additional pressure on markets. Brent crude futures ( BZ=F ) rose to $112 per barrel, while WTI crude ( CL=F ) reached $104 per barrel.
Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) prices tumbled more than 2% as crypto assets were rattled following a $6.3 billion hack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, marking the largest heist of its kind in history.
Following Friday's stock market meltdown, Truist chief investment officer Keith Lerner offered some perspective to those who may be uneasy checking their portfolios this afternoon.
He explained that the pullback has largely been driven by high expectations for tech earnings, investors becoming more discerning about AI returns on investment, and rising borrowing costs.
But while the tech volatility may continue, Lerner laid out reasons to believe this could just be a reset:
The weakness has been narrow: Tech and communication services were the only sectors to fall in October, reflecting a sharp rotation rather than broad selling of the entire market.
Additional downside is possible, but models indicate that stocks won't fall apart completely: According to Lerner, a "combination of historical pullbacks, valuation, and technical support suggests potential downside of roughly 2% to 8% for tech from current levels."
Tech now looks discounted: As Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi pointed out for Alphabet this morning, tech price-to-earnings ratios have fallen. Lerner notes that tech now trades at a lower forward valuation than consumer staples and industrials, despite having the strongest estimated earnings growth for next year.
Pullbacks are normal: "Since the bull market began in October 2022, the S&P 500 has gained approximately 111%, tech has advanced roughly 230%, and
semiconductors have risen more than 380%. Against that backdrop, tech's current 10% decline does not appear abnormal relative to prior pullbacks during this bull market," Lerner wrote.
The bottom line, according to Lerner: "The corrective process may not be complete, but the weight of the evidence suggests the longer-term tech uptrend remains intact."
US stocks plunged Friday as disappointing earnings from tech giants fueled a rout in artificial intelligence stocks, pushing the Nasdaq Composite to its worst day since June 5.
The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 2.8% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1.2%, or over 600 points, while those on the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 1.8%.
The selling intensified after earnings from Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) raised fresh concerns about the enormous cost of the AI boom. The rout followed a sharp decline in Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) on Thursday.
Friday's close marks October as the worst month for the Nasdaq Composite since March 2025, with the index losing 5.3% in gains. The S&P 500 fell 1.2%, while the Dow rose 1.5%.
Hackers behind Binance's estimated $6.3 billion hack are moving stolen funds across blockchains in ways some investigators have never seen before, raising questions about whether artificial intelligence is helping them cover their tracks.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said Friday that investigators observed thousands of transactions in a short period, suggesting the attackers are using automation to obscure the movement of stolen funds.
"Our investigators are observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit," Chainalysis said in a social media post .
It's too early to know whether AI is involved. Automated cryptocurrency transactions are not new, and investigators have yet to establish whether AI played any role in the attack itself.
Stocks fell to session lows in afternoon trading as the technology ( XLK ) sector took a hit.
The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 3.3% headed for its worst day since June. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 2.1%.
Crypto assets continued to slide, with bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) prices tumbling after a $6.3 billion hack of the cryptocurrency exchange Binance, marking the largest heist of its kind in history.
Two members of the Federal Reserve suggested Friday that interest rates need to move higher to push down inflation, Yahooo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports:
St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said he thinks inflation is too high and broad-based, and that the Fed needs to act "soon," otherwise higher prices will persist.
Richmond Fed president Tom Barkin also suggested that the central bank needs to raise rates further to bring down inflation in the face of strong demand. The question is by how much.
The Fed voted in a split decision this week to hold rates steady even as inflation has moved higher. A day later, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up in September , solidifying expectations for an interest rate hike in December
Analysts spent last week raising their SpaceX ( SPCX ) price targets. Investors spent it selling the stock.
SpaceX stock fell about 5% Friday, extending a slide that has erased more than $400 billion in market value since its high on Oct. 6, when the company was worth more than $2.3 trillion. It's now worth less than $2 trillion.
The slide has wiped out SpaceX's post-earnings jump. The stock rose about 8% on Oct. 21 after third quarter results beat Wall Street's forecasts and has since lost more than $250 billion in value.
Then came the lockup. About 1.3 billion shares became free to sell on Oct. 22, and SpaceX held above $140 in the sessions that followed. On Friday, it broke below that level.
A close below $135 would be SpaceX's lowest since Aug. 24, and the next floor below that is the summer low near $107. To turn things around, bulls first need to reclaim about $147, which would put SpaceX back above $2 trillion, and then its $150 first-day open.
The turnaround at Burger King in the US continues to sizzle, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports.
Burger King's US comparable sales increased a stunning 8.4% in the third quarter, parent company Restaurant Brands International ( QSR ) said in its third quarter earnings release this week.
"I think people still look at fast food as a treat, and they want to treat themselves once in a while, and when they want to treat themselves, they don't want to compromise. They don't want to say, 'Well, I'm going to go get the cheap meal. Or the least expensive product, or the lowest-quality product.' They want to feel like they are treating themselves and they're being treated well," Burger King US president Tom Curtis said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned Friday that ongoing global crises threaten energy and food supplies, trade and freedom of navigation as G20 foreign ministers gathered in Atlanta.
"We are tasked, on behalf of the nations that we serve, to work together with one another to coordinate responses to emerging crises and to protect our shared interests," Rubio said in opening remarks, according to Reuters.
"We can help set the context for expanded geopolitical stability and the broader economic prosperity agenda that our leaders will tackle."
The meeting comes as the ongoing war with Iran has raised concerns about global energy supplies and shipping.
Reuters contributed to this report.
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Friday that President Donald Trump has been "very upfront" with Americans about the impact the war with Iran is having on fuel prices , calling the increase a "short-term consequence."
"If you also look at what the president has done for our energy industry, he is bringing down the price of gasoline and diesel," Leavitt said during an appearance on "The Story with Martha MacCallum."
"Of course, he's been very upfront with voters in Iowa and all across the country about what the war in Iran is doing," she said. "It's a short-term consequence. But overall, his energy policy will bring gas prices and diesel costs down again."
Leavitt contrasted Trump's energy agenda with Democrats' policies.
"If you look at it in contrast to what the Democrats want to do, they want to completely shut down and phase out our country from fossil fuels, which will jack up energy costs, which will not be good for anyone in rural America or anywhere in America," she said.
Yemen's government said Friday that Iran-aligned Houthis launched ballistic missile attacks targeting Aden International Airport and the presidential palace complex in the city.
A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces said the Houthis targeted the airport and the Maashiq presidential palace complex, according to Reuters.
Officials did not immediately provide details on casualties or damage, or say whether the missiles struck their intended targets.
Reuters contributed to this report.
Streamer Hasan Piker compared pro-Israel Jewish voters in Michigan to the Ku Klux Klan during a livestream Thursday.
Piker made the comparison while discussing campaign volunteers for Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed canvassing a Jewish neighborhood outside Detroit.
He called it "the wildest door-knocking operation of all time," saying volunteers were trying to convince "one of the more Zionist, wealthy districts in the country to vote for a Muslim anti-Zionist."
"Brave soldiers — all of 'em," Piker said.
“This is the equivalent of going to that, like, Klan, KKK neighborhood to stump for like a Black candidate,” he said. “... The supremacist attitude underlying in their worldview is identical.”
He added, “If you are pro-Israel to the degree that you are making a big fuss about never voting for Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim anti-Zionist, yes, it is the equivalent. ... It’s racial supremacy. It’s Jewish supremacy.”
Germany's Foreign Office said Friday that most G20 nations agree that Iran must return to negotiations.
"Most of the [G20] share our view: [Iran] must come to the negotiating table, the [Houthis] must cease their attacks, and [Russia] must stop driving global [food security] towards collapse with its attacks in the Black Sea," the account wrote on X.
The statement came as G20 nations gathered amid heightened tensions in the Middle East.
President Donald Trump said Friday that Iran wants "to talk" as the war stretches into its eighth month.
"They want to talk. They keep talking," Trump told reporters.
The president claimed that Iran is struggling to pay its security forces as the conflict continues.
"Look, they're not paying their soldiers, they're not paying their police. They're, you know, they're in a lot of trouble," he said.
The president also described the conflict as "not a typical war" and said Washington is spending "very little money, relatively speaking."
Trump also defended the cost of the U.S. campaign, saying the money was spent "in order to get rid of a nuclear weapon," while arguing U.S. actions in Venezuela have more than offset the expense.
"Any money we've spent in Iran, we've more than made up for with what we did in Venezuela," he said.
The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh on Friday again warned Americans in Saudi Arabia to exercise extreme caution around airports amid ongoing Houthi attacks and travel disruptions.
In its latest security alert, the embassy reiterated that non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members were ordered to leave Saudi Arabia effective Oct. 23 due to "safety risks."
"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area," the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh wrote on X.
U.S. citizens were also warned of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions.
"Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia," the post added.
October saw the highest number of reported maritime incidents in the Strait of Hormuz region since the U.S.-Iran conflict began , according to data released by the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
The UKMTO report shows incidents across the Strait of Hormuz, Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman climbed to their highest monthly level in October, with 144 total events reported since Feb. 28.
"UKMTO reports only incidents verified through primary sources; additional incidents are known but cannot beindependently verified," the agency noted.
An Iranian lawmaker has called for Tehran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and change its nuclear doctrine amid the ongoing war with the U.S. and Israel.
Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of Iran's parliament, said the country has already paid a "heavy" price through war and sanctions.
"Now that we have paid the heavy costs of war and sanctions, it is time for the Iranian nation to withdraw from the NPT treaty and change the nuclear doctrine," Nabavian wrote on X.
Pakistan's military said Friday it is "cautiously optimistic" about efforts to mediate between Iran and the U.S. after its army chief made his second visit to Tehran this month.
Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan's army chief and a key mediator in efforts to de-escalate the Iran war, traveled to Tehran on Monday alongside senior Saudi and Turkish officials, according to Reuters.
"Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course," military spokesman Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether Munir's visits were a positive sign, the outlet reported.
Reuters contributed to this report.
The Israel Defense Forces said Friday that it destroyed two weapons storage facilities used by the Iran-backed Hamas terrorist group, as well as at least six of its members.
The IDF said the facilities were "used by Hamas' military wing in the Al-Bureij area and in the Gaza City area" of the Gaza Strip, and stored dozens of weapons including "RPGs, explosive devices, rockets, Kalashnikov rifles, grenades, magazines and additional combat equipment."
Two strikes on Wednesday in Khan Younis and Rafah left four Hamas members dead, according to the IDF.
It also said Friday that it killed "Ihab Jamil Abu Taqiya, a squad commander in Hamas’ military wing who was involved in holding numerous hostages in Hamas captivity at the beginning of the war," and "Ibrahim Gihad Muhammad Abu Oshaiba, a platoon commander in Hamas’ military wing."

articles.title_orig: China Claims GJ-21 Naval UCAV has Flown from Type 076 Sichuan LHD
articles.title_zh: China Claims GJ-21 Naval UCAV has Flown from Type 076 Sichuan LHD
articles.content_orig:
China’s GJ-21 naval Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle (UCAV) has reportedly conducted its first takeoff and landing aboard the Type 076 Sichuan amphibious assault ship, the Chinese military announced on Oct. 30, 2026 . The development was first reported by state news agencies Xinhua and Global Times , and subsequently publicized by the Ministry of National Defense and the official China Military Bugle social media account.
The military described the GJ-21 as the country’s “first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone,” saying that it “recently made its first successful take-off and landing on 076 amphibious assault ship, the ‘Sichuan’.” However, neither the state press nor the military released any official image or video of the actual flight operations.
The development comes as the U.S. Navy advances its own MQ-25 Stingray unmanned aerial refueler program. Primarily designed as a carrier-based tanker, the MQ-25 will also provide a secondary maritime intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capability. The Stingray is expected to help mature the technologies and operational concepts needed for unmanned carrier aviation, laying the groundwork for the Navy’s future Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) fleet.
The GJ-21 has so far been associated with the Type 076, but future operations from conventional aircraft carriers have also been suggested, with speculation about the drone eventually operating from Fujian, China’s newest carrier. In our previous reports, we have assessed that the GJ-21 could provide an amphibious task group with an embarked unmanned ISR-and-strike capability, potentially extending reconnaissance and precision-attack options beyond the ship’s immediate surroundings
China’s first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone “GJ-21” recently made its first successful take-off and landing on 076 amphibious assault ship, the “Sichuan” (Hull 51).
This is another significant breakthrough in the development of China’s amphibious assault ship, indicating that the Chinese Navy now has the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms.
Launched on December 27, 2024, the Sichuan (Hull 51) is the first vessel of Type 076 amphibious assault ships designed and developed independently by China. It incorporates the automatic carrier landing guidance system, new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested landing technology, and is capable of carrying fixed-wing unmanned aircraft, helicopters, and amphibious equipment, etc.
Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan warship has been steadily conducting various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability tests.

The official China Military Bugle account emphasized the PLA Navy’s “capability to operate fixed wing stealth drones from maritime combat platforms.” The statement added:
“[The Sichuan] incorporates the automatic carrier landing guidance system, new integrated power system, and electromagnetic catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested landing technology, and is capable of carrying fixed-wing unmanned aircraft, helicopters, and amphibious equipment, etc. Since its first sea trial in November 2025, the Sichuan warship has been steadily conducting various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability tests.”
🇨🇳Type 076 + GJ-21 Stealth Drone Swarm🤙
China’s Type 076 amphibious assault ship is being fitted with the GJ-21 stealth carrier-based UAV. Flying-wing design, fluidic thrust vectoring for autonomous carrier landings, electromagnetic catapult launch. Estimated 30 drones per ship, over 2-ton internal payload, ~2,000 km combat radius and 12+ hours endurance.
Extremely low RCS allows deep stealth penetration to clear air defenses, airfields and anti-ship sites before troops even hit the beach. It can also act as loyal wingman with the J-35.
Unlike the US “Lightning Carrier” concept of F-35B on amphibious ships, limited by vertical takeoff payload and range, plus the risk and cost of every manned jet; the Type 076 uses electromagnetic catapults and stealth UAV swarms for higher launch rate, longer reach, better endurance and zero pilot risk.
This upgrades amphibious warfare from bloody beach assaults into non-contact, industrial-scale stealth suppression.
China knows its priority building advanced defense capabilities for the people! Not war!

Global Times additionally quoted Chinese military analyst Song Zongping, who described the GJ-21’s flight operations from the Sichuan as a “global first” and compared it to the U.S. Navy’s X-47B program. “[The] US X-47B carrier-based drone program was designed for aircraft carriers, yet multiple technical constraints led to its cancellation. By contrast, the GJ-21 program has advanced steadily with an efficient development timeline,” Song told GT .
However, the comparison requires some qualification: the X-47B was an experimental demonstrator that successfully completed a series of carrier-aviation milestones before the UCAS-D (Unmanned Combat Air System – Demonstrator) program concluded in 2015. The Navy subsequently redirected its follow-on unmanned-aircraft effort toward the CBARS (Carrier-Based Aerial-Refueling System) aerial-refueling role, which evolved into the MQ-25 Stingray.
Song further added that the GJ-21 may also operate from China’s other EMALS carrier, the Fujian. He argued that this would help “building the technical know-how for China’s third aircraft carrier to host manned-unmanned teaming, expanding the operational modes of carrier strike groups.”

articles.title_orig: 14 New Things Your iPhone Can Do in iOS 27.2
articles.title_zh: 14 New Things Your iPhone Can Do in iOS 27.2
articles.content_orig:
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, bringing enhancements to Siri AI, adding Suggestions in Messages, and sneaking in a string of smaller additions across Photos, Podcasts, Games, Apple TV, and FaceTime.
iOS 27.2 is available to download to your device now via Settings ➝ General ➝ Software Update. Note that some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. Apple maintains a feature availability list with all the details.
Siri AI can now recall your past conversations, so you can ask it about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI features require an iPhone 16 model or later, or an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max.
Siri AI can now draw from more sources when answering, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, and your voicemails. Apple says you'll also get better results from Safari history and Reading List.
Siri AI now supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, in addition to English. Just keep in mind that, as things stand, it's not available in the EU or mainland China.
A new settings menu has been added that lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one list. You can find it in Settings ➝ Siri ➝ Excluded Apps.
Granular text selection lets you select and copy only the part of a Siri response you need, rather than the whole reply.
The new Suggestions in Messages feature aims to help you take quick actions based on the context of a conversation, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner or saving a Reminder. The feature appeared during iOS 27 beta testing but was held back from the initial release , so its arrival has been a good while coming.
Shared Albums in Photos gain three additions. You can now edit captions and comments, the app can avoid adding duplicate photos, and it can display a reminder before an album expires so participants can save important photos and videos.
iOS 27.2 supports SynthID watermarking, which aims to help you identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.
In the Games app, the Friends tab now provides context around friend suggestions, plus it shows you any recent games your friends have played on their player pages.
If you have an Apple TV, you can now create profiles in the account settings section on iPhone and iPad. All you need for a profile is a name, plus whether it's for an adult or a child. Creating a profile for a child limits content to a PG rating by default, but there's a customize option for finer control. You can select age ratings for TV shows and movies that are appropriate for the child based on their age.
Dual Capture is now available in group ‌FaceTime‌ calls, so you can stream ‌FaceTime‌ video content from the front and rear cameras at the same time. On a compatible device running ‌iOS 27‌.2, flipping the camera while on a ‌FaceTime‌ call automatically turns on Dual Capture.
Dual Capture is available on the iPhone 17, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and ‌iPhone Duo‌.
Multiview has been expanded in the Apple TV app to the iPhone, so you can now watch up to four live sports streams at the same time. Multiview works for sports events that come with an ‌Apple TV‌ subscription, so that's Major League Soccer (MLS), Formula 1 (F1) in the U.S., and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders during the Major League Baseball season.
iOS 27.2 adds Apple Pencil USB-C support to the ‌iPhone Duo‌. It also includes support for the Edge Light feature that first appeared in macOS to illuminate your face during video calls.
A new feature of Call Context reminds you that it's your anniversary when you call that special person – as long as you've added the date in the Contacts app. To add an anniversary to a contact, open the Contacts app and select their name. Tap "Edit" in the corner, then tap "add date," and the first suggestion under date is anniversary. Do it now. It could save your marriage...

articles.title_orig: Think tank: 114 companies paid no current federal income tax but still aren’t biggest hit to deficit
articles.title_zh: Think tank: 114 companies paid no current federal income tax but still aren’t biggest hit to deficit
articles.content_orig:
The effective corporate income tax rate is now the lowest it’s been in decades, and a tapering revenue source for the U.S. government is raising concerns among some policy experts.
More than 700 profitable corporations paid 10.4% in current federal income taxes last year, according to a recent report from the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy (ITEP), a progressive think tank—less than half of the 21% statutory federal corporate income tax rate. More than 250 of those companies paid effective tax rates below 7%, and 114 companies—including Tesla , Walt Disney , United Airlines , and DoorDash—paid no current federal income taxes, the report said.
ITEP calculated these tax rates based on analyses of annual financial reports filed to the Securities and Exchange Commission, and not IRS data, which lags behind SEC filings.
Corporate tax revenue has plummeted under the Trump administration, which has ushered in a series of tax breaks meant to boost capital investments, even as corporate profits have soared. Treasury Department data released earlier this month showed about a 15% reduction, about $70 billion, in corporate income tax revenue to $381 billion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30. The drop is part of a more than 25% reduction in corporate tax revenue since 2024, when former President Joe Biden was in office.
Diminishing corporate tax revenue has some policy experts concerned about a ballooning federal deficit and the U.S. government’s ability to fund itself. The Congressional Budget Office projected President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) would add $3.4 trillion to the federal deficit over the next decade, a result of a $4.5 trillion decrease in revenues offset by a $1.1 trillion decrease in spending. Meanwhile, corporate profits have soared to a record $4.7 trillion for the past 12 months through mid-2026, a 17% increase from the prior 12-month period.
Rather than blame the more than 100 companies paying nothing in federal income tax, however, it’s the hundreds of corporations paying a reduced rate that present the bigger threat to tax revenue, according to Matt Gardner, ITEP senior fellow and coauthor of the report. The 706 companies saved a total of $198 billion last year as a result of corporate tax subsidies, while the 114 corporations that paid nothing accounted for a fraction of that.
“There’s a real concentration of profits at the top, and when those companies pay anything less than 21%, that’s really what is knocking a hole in our corporate tax laws right now,” Gardner told Fortune . “Their profits were so huge that their tax avoidance is way more consequential for the federal government’s capacity to function than the zero tax corporations are.”
Though corporate tax breaks have been in action for decades, Trump has taken steps in both of his terms to slash these taxes, beginning in 2018 when he lowered the federal corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21% . OBBBA, passed last July, extended the 21% rate and also made several breaks permanent while adding others, including immediate expensing of domestic research and development costs, as well as 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying business property acquired after January 2025.
Those two breaks are what companies have taken advantage of the most, Gardner noted. The four companies with the largest tax breaks— Alphabet , Microsoft , Amazon , and Meta—saved a collective $46 billion from those two opportunities, according to the report, taking advantage of the exemptions to help fund massive AI infrastructure build-outs .
Meta in particular has attracted scrutiny over how it has taken advantage of the R&D tax break. The tech company reportedly classified its AI data centers as experimental “pilot models,” according to reports cited by senators, which would allow it to receive the tax break. Sens. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), and Peter Welch (D-Vt.) wrote a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg earlier this month demanding answers by Oct. 31 on how the investments Meta is claiming tax breaks for differ from routine costs for equipping data centers.
“The federal research credit can be a useful and necessary tool to support our nation’s innovation economy and cutting-edge research,” the senators wrote. “Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard.”
Meta said it is one of the largest investors in R&D in the U.S., investing more than $200 billion over the past five years and $57 billion just last year.
“Unlike traditional data centers, AI-optimized data centers are inherently new and require extensive testing and experimentation that cannot be simulated in order to get the design and build right,” a Meta spokesperson told Fortune in a statement. “This is precisely the kind of domestic investment Congress encouraged when it established these tax incentives decades ago.”
Gardner expects this trend of leaning heavily on depreciation and R&D bonuses to continue because of the permanent features of the tax law Trump implemented.
“There’s every reason to expect this to be the new normal going forward, unless the next Congress, the next presidential administration, decides to reverse them,” he said.
One school of thought in favor of higher corporate taxes argues that greater revenue can reduce the deficit, which can lower interest rates and accelerate borrowing and subsequent growth. But other policy experts have called foul on increasing corporate taxes, instead arguing higher taxes would disincentivize investments and throttle America’s competitiveness on the global stage, ultimately weakening opportunities for economic growth.
Adam Michel, director of tax policy studies at the libertarian Cato Institute, argued in an April Substack post that the R&D credit has had bipartisan support since its 1981 introduction under the Economic Recovery Tax Act. The law, nicknamed the Kemp-Roth tax cut for Rep. Jack Kemp (R-N.Y.) and Sen. William Roth (R-Del.), was part of then-President Ronald Reagan’s efforts to build a coalition of more conservative Democrats to support his spending cuts. He argued a depreciation tax break would bolster economic growth, as it lowers immediately taxable income but not the nominal amount of tax payments, giving businesses more of an opportunity to invest.
Tax breaks “don’t reveal a scandal,” Michel wrote. “They are a list of popular, bipartisan policies. Companies using them are doing what the law intends, often for good reason.”
Sasha Rogelberg is a reporter and former editorial fellow on the news desk at Fortune , covering retail and the intersection of business and popular culture.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27.2 adds two FaceTime features, including a personal favorite
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.2 adds two FaceTime features, including a personal favorite
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.2 adds new features to Messages , Podcasts , Photos , and more—including some easy-to-miss upgrades to FaceTime. Here’s what’s new.
Dual Capture was added to FaceTime in iOS 27 and quickly became one of my favorite features. Rather than having to choose between showing your face or the rear camera view, Dual Capture lets you show both at once.
iOS 27.2 expands Dual Capture to work on all video calls, even with groups. Previously the feature was limited to one-on-one calls.
If you have an iPhone 17 or newer, all you have to do on a video call is hit the ‘Flip’ button, and by default both the front and back camera will be activated.
It’s a huge upgrade to the FaceTime experience, and especially great if, like in my case, you have young kids running around and want to let grandparents see them and you at the same time.
The only drawback: everyone in the call needs to have iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27 installed.
iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime more accessible by adding support for third-party sign language interpreters and live captioning.
Inside the three-dot icon, you’ll find a ‘Sign Language’ button that lets you pick an installed VRS (Video Relay Service) app for direct access to an interpreter. The app will appear as a participant tile in the call with a “Waiting for Interpreter” status, then your interpreter’s name will display after they join.
For third-party live captioning, Apple has a step-by-step support document here that outlines the process. You can also optionally stick with the existing built-in Live Captions feature to have your iPhone add automatic captions. It’s available from Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ FaceTime ⇾ Live Captions.
If you have an iPhone Duo, iOS 27.2 also introduced a new Edge Light feature that works across multiple video calling apps, including FaceTime.
Edge Light works just like on the Mac , adding a ring of light around the iPhone Duo display to better illuminate your face on calls. It’s a built-in alternative to using a physical ring light.
To enable the feature, open Control Center while on a FaceTime call then hit ‘FaceTime Controls’ and tap ‘Edge Light.’ Once enabled, you can adjust settings like the intensity and color temperature.
Have you tried any of iOS 27.2’s new FaceTime features? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_orig: ‘Asleep at the wheel’: Wallace slams Trump over China spy report involving Nvidia CEO
articles.title_zh: ‘Asleep at the wheel’: Wallace slams Trump over China spy report involving Nvidia CEO
articles.content_orig:
Wallace shared “shocking” new reporting that she said may show Trump is “setting America up to be a great loser on the world stage.”
MS NOW’s Nicolle Wallace shared “shocking” new reporting from The New York Times, which she said could show that President Donald Trump is “asleep at the wheel in protecting U.S. national security.”
On Thursday’s “Deadline: White House,” Wallace discussed the Times’ “blockbuster” report about a Chinese businesswoman’s close relationship with Jensen Huang , president and CEO of Nvidia, the world’s most dominant leader in artificial intelligence chips. U.S. officials concluded the woman was a Chinese intelligence asset, according to the report.
“The discovery that Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access to Mr. Huang, one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump’s, set off alarms at the White House,” the Times reported.
“What happened next,” Wallace said, “is the stuff of international political scandals.” The Times said Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings but chose not to act. He had “been wary of disrupting Nvidia’s chip sales, which are helping to drive the economy and the stock market, and of further complicating the trading relationship with China,” the report read.
“Donald Trump — the man who claims that no one is tougher on China than he is — does nothing,” Wallace said of the president’s reported inaction. She described “panic among our intelligence agencies as Trump sat by as a Chinese spy got dangerously close to the CEO of America’s most valuable company.”
Nvidia denied that its CEO had been targeted in a spy plot. The company told the Times that “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected” and that he “talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” The White House, the CIA and the National Security Agency declined to comment, according to the Times.
Wallace also pointed to “close financial ties” between Trump and Nvidia that were described in the report. A person familiar with the matter told the Times that Nvidia donated at least $20 million to Trump’s White House ballroom fund. Earlier this month, Trump disclosed that he bought up to $1.6 million worth of Nvidia stock and sold up to $1 million in August.
Wallace said the report exposed a gap between Trump’s public statements and private behavior.
“Earlier this year, he cited the importance of protecting America’s technological secrets and beating China in the AI arms race as his entire rationale for why AI can’t and should not be regulated ever,” she said.
By that logic, Wallace said, Trump is “setting America up to be a great loser on the world stage, as he imperils U.S. national security in a matter that’s deeply entangled in his own bottom line.”
You can watch Wallace’s full comments in the clip at the top of the page.
