articles.title_orig: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
articles.title_zh: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
articles.content_orig:
American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.
Last week’s global release of “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” came days before the Oct. 29 anniversary of the disaster in the South Korean capital’s nightlife district of Itaewon, where a crowd of tens of thousands of partygoers surged beyond control in a narrow alley, causing nearly 160 deaths.
The game, which takes place amid a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, features about 10 seconds of heavily edited footage of the tragedy to illustrate what the aftermath of a Pyongyang attack might look like, though it does not refer to the Itaewon crowd crush directly.
Groups representing families of the crowd crush victims had demanded that the footage be removed, saying it was appalling that the game had directly reproduced actual scenes of people performing CPR “while victims lay on the cold streets amid chaos and desperation.”
“If the game developer has even the slightest sense of respect and empathy for the victims of the Itaewon disaster, it should promptly take corrective action,” the Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee said in a joint statement Friday.
The California-based game publisher, Activision, apologized in a statement and said the footage would be completely removed through a game update scheduled for release Nov. 12.
“This game is a fictional work created to provide a realistic and immersive experience,” the company said, according to the South Korean public broadcaster MBC. “In using actual news footage in the game, we never intended to evoke any tragic incident, including the Itaewon disaster, or to trivialize the suffering associated with such tragedies.”
The controversy came as grieving families are still waiting for answers about authorities’ failure to prevent the disaster four years ago. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged in the investigation, which is still underway, while three former police officers have been jailed.
On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed that his government would “uncover the truth.”
“On that day, when what should have been a joyful autumn night turned into the scene of a horrific tragedy, the state was nowhere to be found,” he said in a statement on X.
Lee Jin Woo, whose younger sister was 28 when she died in the crowd crush, told NBC News that he had played the new “Call of Duty” game and didn’t notice the Itaewon footage at first.
“But after hearing about it and thinking it over, I began to realize the footage looked very similar,” said Lee, who works at a South Korean gaming company.
“The more I thought about it, the more I felt betrayed as a gamer,” he said. “After all, it was a game company and a game series that I had liked.”
The game’s premise, in which South Korean conscripts are thrust into defending their country alongside American soldiers after a North Korean invasion, has been controversial since before it was available to play.
Though the “Call of Duty” invasion is fictional, it draws on North Korea’s real-life capture of Seoul in 1950 during the Korean War. The conflict ended in 1953 with an armistice instead of a peace treaty, and the two Koreas remain technically at war.
Tensions between the North and South have escalated in recent weeks, with the two countries embroiled in a standoff along their heavily militarized border. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has rebuffed diplomatic outreach from Washington and Seoul as he continues to advance his nuclear and ballistic missile programs.
“Ultimately, whether we’re talking about an actual war or the Itaewon disaster, both involve the suffering of real people,” Lee Mi Hyun, a director at the Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee, told NBC News in an interview.
“They’re turning that suffering into entertainment,” she said. “It’s an approach that seems to show absolutely no empathy for the people who experienced that suffering.”
Some South Korean lawmakers say the game should be taken as a warning.
“We need to pay attention to the question it raises,” Han Dong-hoon, an opposition legislator, said last week in a Facebook post. “If that day were to come again, would we be ‘prepared’?”
The game has also been defended by members of Lee’s governing Democratic Party such as Kim Han Kyu, who said there was “nothing wrong with playing a game set against the backdrop of North Korea’s nuclear weapons.”
“We are still technically under an armistice, aren’t we?” he said Thursday in a Facebook post. “Wouldn’t it be even stranger if no games depicted a war against North Korea?”
Others have used the game to criticize Lee’s conciliatory approach to North Korea, with opposition lawmaker Ahn Cheol Soo suggesting last week that the South Korean president try playing the game to correct his “naïve judgment” about the North Korean threat.
With its “Call of Duty” franchise struggling to sustain interest in recent years, the Microsoft-owned Activision used “Modern Warfare 4” to deliver what fans loved about its previous games: a hyperrealistic military shooter.
“I don’t think we were happy with every aspect of last year’s game, and we heard the feedback loud and clear,” Activision Chief Marketing Officer Tyler Bahl told “The Game Business Show” earlier this month .
“With ‘Modern Warfare 4,’ we’ve tried to adjust based on that feedback. It’s getting back to a grounded military shooter. Making it cinematic, making it authentic and bringing that edge back that ‘Call of Duty’ is known for,” he said.
That approach appears to have worked. As of Friday, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” was the top-selling game in both South Korea and the United States on Steam , an online PC game distribution platform.
In its review, gaming website IGN said it was a “much-needed reminder of what ‘Call of Duty’ can be at its best, even if it can’t fully recapture the heights of its glory days.”
Mithil Aggarwal is a Hong Kong-based reporter/producer for NBC News.
Stella Kim is an NBC News freelance producer based in Seoul.

articles.title_orig: ExxonMobil and Chevron report blowout profits as Trump touts benefits of high oil prices
articles.title_zh: ExxonMobil and Chevron report blowout profits as Trump touts benefits of high oil prices
articles.content_orig:
It’s a good time to be an oil company.
The two largest U.S. oil companies, ExxonMobil and Chevron, on Friday reported blowout profits that easily beat expectations as oil prices remain sharply elevated because of the U.S. war with Iran.
ExxonMobil reported a profit that doubled from the same period last year, while Chevron’s earnings surged more than 180% from a year earlier.
As part of the bumper returns, Exxon said it was increasing the dividend it pays to investors.
The returns at both companies came as the price of oil surged beyond $100 per barrel and has remained there for months. On Friday, prices accelerated again, with Brent oil trading closing just under $118 per barrel.
The highest level that Brent reached since the United States and Israel launched the Iran war in late February was $126, which it is now approaching again.
Since the start of the year, Exxon shares have risen 52%, and Chevron shares have returned 50%.
Overnight, another major oil company, BP, reported that its profit skyrocketed to an 18-year high.
The average price of regular gasoline has soared 40% for consumers since the war broke out. Soaring prices continue to pressure consumers ahead of the midterm elections, where voters have repeatedly said that prices and inflation are primary concerns.
In 2024, Donald Trump repeatedly pledged to drive energy costs down . “My plan will cut energy prices in half or more than that within 12 months of taking office,” the then-candidate said in September 2024, while adding that it would mean “gasoline below $2 a gallon.”
As of Friday, the average gasoline price is currently more than double that.
In recent rallies on the campaign trail, the president has celebrated the higher oil and gas profits. “I wonder if I should say this,” Trump mused aloud during a rally Oct. 24, before saying “our country is making hundreds of billions of dollars because of what’s happened in the Middle East.”
Trump touts U.S. oil business making ‘hundreds of billions’
“My people said, ‘Please don’t mention that, sir,’ because people are paying a little higher,” Trump continued. “But what we’ve done for this country, we’re making money like this country has never made before.”
“I don’t give a damn: I’m going to say it. We’re making a freaking fortune.”
The higher prices are also a result of the war between Ukraine and Russia following President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion of his neighbor in 2022.
“There’s a lot of disruption happening in the world,” ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods told CNBC on Friday morning . “What you’re finding is because of the closure” in the Strait of Hormuz, “shipping has to find new routes around to continue to deliver the products that society desperately needs.”
“About half of Russia’s refinery capacity has been taken out from the Ukraine bombing,” he added.
“That shortage of refining capacity and availability to the world is what’s driving product prices as high as it is, and frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here because it is so critical to economic growth,” Woods continued.
Since the start of the year, the average nationwide price for diesel fuel has risen 78%. New York-traded diesel futures have soared 130% since the start of the year, likely indicating more price rises could still come at the pump.
Both Exxon and Chevron said that they were running their refineries at maximum output to continue making as much diesel as possible.
Trump has taken specific note of the impact that diesel could have on the economy. The administration has quickly issued multiple orders and policies in an attempt to bring prices down.
The president signed an order allowing more widespread use of an off-road dyed variety of diesel, has pressured European allies to release more of the diesel reserves into the global market, and has announced a deal with Putin for some of that country’s diesel supplies.
Trump’s latest move came last week, when he announced $150 million in Defense Production Act funding to “expand petroleum production, storage, and logistics at refineries across.”
The moves have not meaningfully brought prices down.
On Friday, Woods said his refineries were already being pushed to the limit. “We are at record levels of utilization for our refineries,” he said on CNBC.
“If you look at North America, we produce record volumes of diesel. That’s all been a function of trying to drive more product into the marketplace to meet that demand and to drive costs down.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: Binance Hack Sends Crypto Stocks Tumbling
articles.title_zh: Binance Hack Sends Crypto Stocks Tumbling
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Exec Edge Editorial Staff
In the third quarter of 2026, Coinbase Global, Inc. (NASDAQ: COIN) reported total revenue of $1.2 billion, net income of $719 million, adjusted EBITDA of $333 million and adjusted net income of $78 million, per the earnings presentation .
Coinbase's total revenue was stable from Q2 2026, and transaction revenue was $590 million, per the earnings presentation . Net income was $719 million.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $333 million, up 60% Q/Q, marking Coinbase's 15th consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Coinbase described the drivers this way: "$1.2B total revenue was flat Q/Q against a backdrop of a decline in Total Market Crypto Trading Volume (-10% Q/Q) and flat Average Crypto Market Capitalization," and "Transaction revenue declined 1% Q/Q as Crypto Asset Volatility reached multi-year lows."
49% of net revenue came from Subscription and Services revenue in Q3 2026, which was $570 million, per the earnings presentation . That was within Coinbase's Q3 outlook of $500 million to $580 million, and up from a 41% share of net revenue in Q3 2025.
The lines inside Subscription and Services revenue were stablecoin revenue of $307 million (up 5% Q/Q), blockchain rewards of $86 million (up 3%), interest and finance fee income of $69 million (up 4%) and other Subscription and Services revenue of $109 million (down 4%). Coinbase describes this part of the business as providing "diversification and support independent of transaction revenue."
Paid Coinbase One subscribers grew 24% Y/Y to an all-time high in Q3 2026, per the earnings presentation .
Coinbase One is Coinbase's paid subscription product. Paid Coinbase One Subscribers have 3.5x higher average revenue per user, 4.2x higher balances per user and 50%+ higher long-term trading retention than non-subscribers.
Prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue (ARR) in Q3 2026, and daily traders (DAU) grew more than 60% Q/Q, per the release .
Prediction markets revenue has seen 82% quarterly compound growth since launch, and Coinbase points to a diversified "contract mix with non-sports categories showing strong growth through seasonally slower sports months." In the release, Brian Armstrong, Co-Founder and CEO, said: "Prediction markets have been one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase history, growing even through slower sports months driven by crypto contracts where we have a strong right to win."
Derivatives sit within what Coinbase calls the Everything Exchange, which it describes as bringing "more markets and products into one place, expanding the ways customers can trade." In Q3, Coinbase recorded $963 billion in crypto derivatives trading volume, down 6% Q/Q against an 11% decline for the market, and a fourth consecutive quarter of derivatives market share gains.
Average USDC held in Coinbase products was $22 billion in Q3 2026, an all-time high for the 14th consecutive quarter and up 49% Y/Y, per the release .
Stablecoin revenue was $307 million, per the earnings presentation . Coinbase groups USDC under its Stablecoins and Payments priority. Over the past year, Coinbase captured approximately 50% of all USDC economics, with "onchain partnerships and deeper product integration driving greater USDC adoption."
Coinbase's Q4 outlook, as stated in the earnings presentation , is about $165 million in transaction revenue quarter-to-date through October 25; $550 million to $630 million in Subscription and Services revenue; transaction expenses in the mid-teens as a percentage of net revenue; $1.007 billion to $1.157 billion in adjusted expenses; and about $240 million in stock-based compensation. Coinbase cautions against extrapolating the quarter-to-date transaction revenue.

Watch the full series of Arkanaut on Warhammer TV now
The third and final instalment of the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar animation Arkanaut is live now, and available to watch on Warhammer TV . Warhammer+ subscribers can stream it at their leisure. If you’re not signed up yet, check out this trailer to see what you’re missing:
This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.
Warning – if you’ve not watched the first two episodes yet, there are spoilers ahead!
Episode 3 opens with the remaining Arkanauts at the mercy of a new adversary – a Helsmith of the Fallen Ancestor Hashut. This first animated view of the Bullfather’s followers gives us a glimpse at just how divergent this culture is from their Kharadron cousins, and specifically, their perspective on power and technology.
The Kharadron Overlords and the Helsmiths of Hashut have a common lineage in the Khazalid empire of old – a culture that still endures relatively unchanged as the Khazalite Holds . The technology of their ancestors revolved around runes and the innate resonant magic of stone.
Both the Kharadron and the Helsmiths have since abandoned this technology. The Kharadron as there are not many rocks kicking about in the sky, and the Helsmiths as “harmony with nature” is not really how they roll.
Kharadron technology revolves around the use of a lighter-than-air material called Aether-gold, also called “the Breath of Grungni”. This powers not only their airships, but also their suits, weapons, and cities. In fact, without it, the entire Kharadron civilisation would quite literally come crashing to the ground. So the Kharadron dedicate much of their efforts to the finding and extraction of this valuable resource.
The Helsmiths have harnessed an altogether more dangerous material. Their technology runs on the distilled soul-essence of captured and processed daemons. As you might imagine, this is a volatile and unpredictable energy source, but incredibly powerful.
The Helsmiths believe that they are untainted by the use of this power, and that they have the willpower and fortitude to endure contact with this Chaotic essence. Their malevolent demeanor, sprouting tusks, and the fact that many of their most prolific magic users slowly petrify with use of this magical power source is entirely unrelated, probably.
This daemonic essence powers vast forges, which have become the greatest engines of industry in the Mortal Realms. These create vast arsenals of weapons and constructs for the Helsmiths and their dubious allies, taint the land about them, and drive the forced evacuation of other local denizens like skaven, orruks, and Gloomspite Gitz.
The forge in Arkanaut is a recently repurposed duardin hold that the Helsmiths have claimed and desecrated (as they see it, they’ve just retaken a piece of their ancestral heritage and put it to use again). There are some great shots of the forge in this episode, inspired by the custom scenery created to accompany the recent Helsmiths of Hashut battletome .
There is one more power source at play in this episode, of course.
In episode 1 , the Arkanauts harpooned themselves a Stormcast soul and trapped it inside a jury-rigged aether-tank, intending to sell it back to its brethren at a fair and reasonable price (or possibly another party at a less reasonable price, depending on market conditions).
Now the Helsmiths have the soul and we’re fairly sure they aren’t planning to use it for anything good…

articles.title_orig: Wall Street's Next Blockbuster Stock Split Has Arrived -- The Stock Has Gained 3,050% Since Its 2025 Debut and Still More Upside Ahead, According to Wall Street
articles.title_zh: Wall Street's Next Blockbuster Stock Split Has Arrived -- The Stock Has Gained 3,050% Since Its 2025 Debut and Still More Upside Ahead, According to Wall Street
articles.content_orig:
Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shifted the tech landscape, minting a string of stock winners along the way. One of those is Sandisk ( SNDK -13.47% ) . It's been less than a year since it was spun off from Western Digital in early 2025. In the short time since its debut, Sandisk has become a Wall Street darling, as it supplies memory chips used to underpin AI.
The company's impressive business performance has fueled a surge in its stock price. Sandisk shares have surged 378% thus far in 2026 (as of this writing), and are up 4553% over the past year and 3,050% since its spin-off.
In conjunction with its fiscal 2027 first-quarter financial report, Sandisk announced plans to split its stock for the first time since its debut. This long-rumored announcement has sparked a wave of interest in the semiconductor stock .
Let's take a look at the details, the company's recent results, and why Wall Street thinks there is still upside ahead.
Image source: The Motley Fool.
After the market close on Thursday, Sandisk announced that its board of directors had approved an 8-for-1 stock split. "The stock split will be effected through an amendment to Sandisk's Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation," the company noted in its earnings report.
Shareholders of record as of Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, will receive an additional seven shares of stock for each share they own. Those shares will be distributed after the close of business on Thursday, Nov. 19. The stock is expected to begin split-adjusted trading when the market opens on Friday, Nov. 20.
As is typically the case, shareholders won't need to take any action to participate in the stock split. The brokerage or investment bank will handle the details behind the scenes, and shares will be deposited directly into investors' brokerage accounts once the stock split has taken effect.
The process is complex, so the additional shares may not show up immediately after the market close on Nov. 19. The schedule may vary slightly from brokerage to brokerage, and it may take several days for the newly minted shares to appear.
Actual numbers help provide context. For each share of Sandisk stock an investor holds -- currently trading for roughly $1,200 per share (as of this writing) -- post-split, shareholders will own 8 shares worth $150 each.
Sandisk's financial results help illustrate the surging demand for its memory chips. For its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Oct. 2), the company generated revenue of $11 billion, which surged 378% year over year and 23% quarter over quarter. This drove adjusted earnings per share (EPS) that soared more than 40-fold to $49.51.
For context, analysts' consensus estimates were calling for revenue of $10.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $46.67, so the company cleared both hurdles with ease.
Management's commentary was equally revealing. CEO David Goeckeler noted, "We're hearing from our customers that they have underestimated the amount of NAND they need to run their infrastructure." He went on to say that multiple customers have revised their contracts to increase the amount of supply. CFO Luis Visoso went further, noting that "Our [memory] pipeline exceeds our supply throughout the end of the decade."
Investors have expressed concerns about the durability of AI demand and the emerging potential for competition from China, but Sandisk has taken steps to ensure its windfall continues. The company has shifted to long-term supply agreements with major customers, locking them into minimum prices, with the average duration of the contract lasting four years or longer.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/30/26
Wall Street is bullish about Sandisk's future prospects. Of the 25 analysts who offered an opinion in October, 84% rate it a buy or strong buy. Furthermore, Wall Street's average price target for the stock is about $2,143, implying additional upside of 85%.
Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes is far more bullish than his Wall Street colleagues, with a buy rating and $3,600 price target -- the highest on Wall Street -- suggesting the stock could triple from here.
He cites strong demand for High-Bandwidth Flash memory, firm NAND pricing, and strong free cash flow as the basis for his bullish thesis. Reitzes believes Sandisk can buy back as much as $100 billion in stock over the next three years.
The stock has fallen more than 50% from its peak in late June, fueled by concerns about the resilience of AI demand and the potential for emerging competition from China. However, Sandisk now trades for less than 16 times earnings and 5 times forward earnings.
For investors who believe, as I do, that this is just the beginning for AI, Sandisk stock is a compelling buy.

articles.title_orig: Police Investigate Former Prince Andrew and Epstein’s Time at Balmoral, Royal Estate in Scotland
articles.title_zh: Police Investigate Former Prince Andrew and Epstein’s Time at Balmoral, Royal Estate in Scotland
articles.content_orig:
Force says it has received ‘information’ on pair’s stay at royal estate as reported guests of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor
Detectives in Scotland are investigating Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s stay at Balmoral castle as reported guests of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor amid allegations that women were trafficked to the royal estate.
Police Scotland said it had received “information” and inquiries were at a “very early stage” into the time the disgraced royal spent with the child sex offender at Balmoral.
The late Epstein, who was convicted in 2008 of soliciting sex from girls, and Maxwell, who was convicted in 2021 of sex trafficking a minor, stayed at Balmoral in 1999.
Pictures previously released by the US Department of Justice appear to show Andrew and Epstein shooting on the estate.
The Daily Express has reported that the inquiries relate to claims that women were trafficked to the estate.
A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We have received information and active inquiries are ongoing, but these are at a very early stage. All inquiries are evidence-led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those inquiries. We would never confirm details of ongoing inquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further.”
Other investigations linked to the release of the Epstein files were ongoing within several forces, including Thames Valley police, the Metropolitan police and Surrey police, the National Police Chiefs’ Council confirmed.
An NPCC spokesperson said: “Identifying any further potential offending, suspects, victims or witnesses is a complex process and will take time, but UK policing remains committed to carrying out a meticulous assessment of the material released by the US Department of Justice.”
There was no national investigation at present, the NPCC said.
The former Duke of York was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office on 19 February this year, his 66th birthday, after allegations he had shared sensitive information with Epstein during his time as a UK trade envoy. He was interviewed under caution before being released under investigation. He denies wrongdoing, with the police investigation continuing.
An email released in a tranche of the Epstein files last year and signed by “A” asked the disgraced British socialite Maxwell for “inappropriate friends”. In one of four emails sent to Maxwell in August 2001 by someone using the name the Invisible Man, the sender told her their “valet” had recently died and they had “left the RN”.
Mountbatten-Windsor left the Royal Navy the month before the email was sent. Another email from the same individual, dated 16 August 2001, said they were at “Balmoral summer camp for the royal family” before asking Maxwell: “Have you found me some inappropriate friends?”
In March 2002, an email from Maxwell to the Invisible Man said she had passed on a message to an unnamed individual, with that message beginning: “I just gave Andrew your telephone no.”
The message from Maxwell to the unidentified person also said “Andrew” would be “very happy” if he did some “two legged sight seeing”.
Andrew was the UK’s special representative for international trade and investment from 2001-11, when he stepped down amid controversy over his friendship with Epstein.
He received no salary for travelling around the world and the UK promoting Britain’s business interests, but criticisms were made about the thousands of pounds spent each year on his expenses and travel costs.
His decision to quit the role came in the same year he was pictured with his arm around his primary accuser, Virginia Giuffre, who said she had been trafficked to the former duke at the home of Maxwell.
Andrew paid Giuffre, a woman he has claimed never to have met, millions of pounds to settle a civil suit in the US in 2022.
Giuffre died by suicide, aged 41, in April 2025.

articles.title_orig: Toyota reveals five new lifted Woodland concepts, including the bZ electric SUV
articles.title_zh: Toyota reveals five new lifted Woodland concepts, including the bZ electric SUV
articles.content_orig:
Toyota introduced a new family of lifted, “adventure-ready” Woodland concepts based on the RAV4, Grand Highlander, Sienna, Crown Signia, and bZ electric SUV.
Toyota is the latest automaker to chase the highly profitable off-road market in the US, with plans to expand its “Woodland” lineup.
Although it already sells Woodland versions of the RAV4, Sienna, bZ, and most recently, the Grand Highlander, Toyota said the new family of concept vehicles is “designed for drivers who see adventure not as a destination, but a way of life.”
Toyota’s North American design studio, CALTY Design Research, designed the concepts to explore how some of its most popular nameplates can be used better on and off the road.
Each vehicle features Horizon Blue exterior paint, inspired by Toyota’s 1960s models, including the Stout, Crown, and Corona.
All new concepts also include an exclusive Woodland badge, plus a lift kit, large over-fenders, satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roof and hood, a roof rack, and cross bars to top it off.
According to Toyota, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-In Hybrid and Sienna Woodland Concepts show how its “electrified and family-focused vehicles take on a more adventurous role.”
The electric Woodland bZ Concept “extends the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery electric future.” Meanwhile, the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept and Crown Signia Woodland Concept bring two distinct models to the lineup, Toyota said.
The company didn’t reveal any powertrain specs or other details, but said the concepts show how capability can take many forms, including PHEV, hybrid, and battery electric.
Toyota’s new Woodland Concepts will be on display at the 2026 SEMA Show, starting on November 3.
To give you an idea, the 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower. That’s an extra 37 hp compared to the standard bZ with AWD.
The bZ Woodland also adds off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and the ability to tow up to 3,500 lbs.
Other rugged upgrades include All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.
The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

articles.title_orig: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later
articles.title_zh: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later
articles.content_orig:
It's been a week since the iPhone Duo was released, and MacRumors videographer Dan Barbera wanted to revisit his review since he's been able to use the Duo for a longer stretch of time.
None of us at MacRumors have had a display crack, and we've seen some AI photos floating around, so it's hard to tell just how many people are actually having problems. iPhone Duos with the hinge issue that causes the display to crack seem to get damaged shortly after purchase, so if you've had an ‌iPhone Duo‌ for the last week and it's still fine, it's not likely to have this defect.
The outer display is small, but Dan finds it useful for checking notifications, replying to messages, and scrolling through apps and websites. He unfolds it for multitasking or longer messages, and is a fan of using the ‌iPhone Duo‌ unfolded in portrait mode for watching videos and using an app at the same time.
He finds the Touch ID fingerprint sensor easy to find, and says Apple Watch unlock is similar to Face ID . The cameras are just okay, and someone who zooms in a lot is probably going to miss having a telephoto lens.
Battery life is between an iPhone 18 Pro and a Pro Max, and for most people, it's likely going to last a full day. Not all apps have been updated for the Duo layout yet, but it's getting better. There's an extension called Wider that extends the Safari window to the edges of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s outer display, and it's a big improvement. We may see other accommodations in the coming months as developers and users get used to the new layout.
Dan says the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is the most excited he's been about an iPhone in a long time, and he plans to keep using it even though he misses having a telephoto lens.
Did you get an ‌iPhone Duo‌? What do you think now that you're a week into using it? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title_orig: North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
articles.title_zh: North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hit late Thursday by what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history , with $6.3 billion in funds impacted and roughly half of those assets frozen.
Customer withdrawals have been temporarily suspended, and co-CEO Richard Teng promised the exchange will cover all losses.
"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said on social media.
Binance said it has money set aside in a Secure Asset Fund for Users to handle extreme cases, such as security breaches.
Here's what you need to know:
Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a separate social media post Friday morning that customer withdrawals should resume within 48 hours.
"We are rebuilding the withdrawal service, and we are not switching it back until it passes rigorous testing," noted Teng on Friday. "We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to the Sunday deadline."
Teng said the hack was not carried out by one person. Initial findings pointed to a compromised laptop, but further review revealed broader security breaches.
"This was a complex attack," Teng said. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers."
The attack has rattled crypto markets and related stocks. Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) tumbled 5% to hover below $77,000 on Friday.
Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether ( ETH-USD ) dropping 4% to around $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also plunged by more than 6%.
Crypto-related stocks traded lower, led by shares of Circle, trading platforms Coinbase ( COIN ) and Robinhood ( HOOD ), and digital-asset Treasury giant Strategy ( MSTR ).
Binance said that about $3 billion in assets have been "frozen on-chain so far."
The frozen assets include over $2 billion in stablecoins. Tether, the world's largest stablecoin issuer, "froze more than 1.567B" of its USDT stablecoin in relation to the hack," CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X . The second-largest issuer, Circle ( CRCL ), froze another $800 million "in coordination with law enforcement," CEO Jeremy Allaire said. World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency venture co-founded by President Trump and his sons, said it froze $27 million of its stablecoin, USD1, associated with the hack, according to CEO Zack Witkoff.
Although details are still emerging, the hack is shaping up to be the largest crypto theft in history, far exceeding the previous record set in February 2025, when attackers stole $1.5 billion from the crypto derivatives exchange ByBit.
Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Elliptic have linked the theft to North Korean hackers, with TRM attributing it "with high confidence" to a group known as TraderTraitor, the same group responsible for last year's Bybit hack.
Elliptic estimated Friday that about 44% of the stolen assets have been frozen, with stablecoins accounting for nearly all of those funds. The firm estimated that attackers still controlled over $3 billion in crypto that token issuers cannot directly freeze.
The hackers appear to have compromised Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure, allowing them to authorize transactions that drained billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains, according to the firms. Binance, in its preliminary stage, has conducted an investigation into the hack, which suggests the incident may have begun with a compromised engineer's laptop. The exchange added that it has found no evidence that wallet passwords were leaked.
North Korean hackers swiped $2 billion in 2025 , bringing the rogue regime's total haul since 2016 through the end of last year to $6.75 billion, according to data from crypto firm Chainalysis.
"This is likely the largest crypto hack on record, but the key distinction is that it does not currently appear to be a solvency event for Binance," Fundstrat head of digital assets Sean Farrell said.
"That meaningfully reduces the risk of a negative feedback loop involving withdrawals, forced selling, tighter credit, and broader deleveraging," he added.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
articles.content_orig:
Get the latest news and updates from Dawn
Pakistan is “cautiously optimistic” about its mediation between Iran and the United States, the military’s spokesman said on Friday in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.
“Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive sign.
“The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Lt Gen Chaudhry.
There were still “powerful spoilers and detractors,” who believed conflict serves them, he added without naming them.
Speaking in Rawalpindi, he declined to say what was discussed or whether the US had backed the trip.
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin joined CDF Munir in Tehran on Monday.
The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Makkah pact, of which both Saudi Arabia and Turkiye are a part and which was signed on August 7, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
The pact has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict.
After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional countries without foreign intervention.
The wording of the pact does not bar new members, Lt Gen Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join.
“Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.
Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, the DG ISPR said that it would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership.
He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy sites of Makkah and Madina.
“We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict,” he added.
Asked if there would now be larger military-led campaigns in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rules, Lt Gen Chaudhry said that was not how the army conducted counter-terrorism.
“Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations… The tempo of the freedom of action of (those) IBOs will further increase,” he said.

articles.title_orig: Apple Music 7.0 for Android rolls out with Liquid Glass redesign
articles.title_zh: Apple Music 7.0 for Android rolls out with Liquid Glass redesign
articles.content_orig:
Following a month of beta testing , Apple Music 7.0 is rolling out with a Liquid Glass redesign for Android, as well as the new icon for the streaming service.
This update starts with a tweaked music note icon in black or white, depending on your device theme, replacing the previous red background. Similarly, the accent color throughout Apple Music is now blue.
The app now has a floating bottom bar that lets you see content above, below, and to the sides. There is a small amount of translucency that primarily allows you to make out solid colors underneath the navigation element. The mini-player gets the same treatment and is no longer docked to the bottom bar. However, compared to iOS, scrolling does not collapse the bar into a more compact version.
Version 7.0 introduces a very modern, edge-to-edge design for Android’s system status and navigation bars.
Top bars across Apple Music have been updated. The page title and overflow menu are now on the same line, while the three-dot icons are no longer themed red and have been placed in circular containers. The Library tab sees a big update with “Edit Pins” and “Edit Categories” now part of the three-dot menu.
Artist pages have been thoroughly redesigned with the background now themed based on the cover image. Matching the iOS design, there’s a prominent play button and info page, while share has been placed in the top-right corner.
The Settings page has also been modernized with better grouping. There are no major changes to Now Playing, which did not see any big updates on iOS.
With a recent release , Apple Music for Android switched to a new versioning system that aligns with iOS. Today’s version 7.0 matches iOS 27 and is now widely rolled out via the Play Store .

articles.title_orig: Gold prices plunge to one-year low below $3,900 as higher oil prices fuel fears of more pain ahead
articles.title_zh: Gold prices plunge to one-year low below $3,900 as higher oil prices fuel fears of more pain ahead
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - The gold market has taken a big hit heading into the weekend, with prices breaking convincingly below $4,000 an ounce and falling to their lowest levels in more than a year.
Gold 's sharp selloff Friday pushed prices to their lowest level since October 6, 2025, when the precious metal touched an intraday low of $3,884.61 an ounce. The latest decline comes as investors brace for another potentially volatile week, with U.S. employment data and the midterm elections expected to provide fresh uncertainty for financial markets.
According to analysts and traders, there is significant frustration in the marketplace as gold faces substantial selling pressure even as the U.S. dollar and bond yields weaken. ( Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.) Traditionally, these two factors should be bullish for the precious metal, as they reduce its opportunity costs.
Spot gold last traded at $3,880 an ounce, down 3.5% on the day; prices are down nearly 3% on the week. Silver is experiencing an even bigger drop, with prices falling below $50 an ounce. Spot silver last traded at $48.95 an ounce, down nearly 6% on the day. Silver prices are down nearly 9% since last Friday, marking their worst weekly decline since early June.
Analysts have said that gold has been unable to find any bullish traction, even with lower bond yields, because of broader concerns in the marketplace.
Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged following its monetary policy meeting Wednesday, the central bank remains committed to bringing inflation down. Looking beyond this week's pause, markets still expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December and through the first quarter of 2027.
Philip Streible, Chief Market Strategist at Blue Line Futures, said that gold will continue to struggle as the ongoing war with Iran keeps oil prices elevated.
“The rule in the markets is that you are supposed to buy the inflation and oil right now is the inflation,” he said.
Streible added that gold performs well when the central bank is forced to cut interest rates to support the economy. However, with the economy expanding by 3.4% in the third quarter, he said the U.S. central bank has plenty of room to raise rates.
“If the economy stays strong the Fed can continue to raise interest rates, which means gold will continue to have a target on its back,” he said.
Simon-Peter Massabni, Head of Business Development at XS.com, said that despite the weakness in the U.S. dollar and lower bond yields, gold is reacting to inflation expectations and the future path of interest rates.
“The decisive factor will be whether incoming economic data prompt markets to reassess the interest-rate outlook, shifting expectations toward a pause in tightening or a resumption of rate cuts. Until then, gold is likely to remain under selling pressure, despite supportive factors that continue to underpin its medium- to long-term outlook,” he said.
“I see three developments that could change the outlook. First, a gradual but clear cooling in the US labor market, reflected in weaker job growth, rising unemployment, and slower wage growth. Second, a sustained decline in inflation, particularly core inflation and price components that capture the pass-through of higher energy costs into broader goods and services. Third, a downward repricing of future interest rate expectations and real yields.”
Looking at gold's technical price action, Waleed Said, Technical Analyst at GivTrade, said that the path of least resistance remains lower. He added that he expects gold prices to eventually test support at $3,800 an ounce.
The latest selloff has also pushed gold significantly below its 200-day moving average, which stands near $4,490 an ounce. With prices trading roughly 13.5% below this long-term trend indicator, the technical picture continues to reflect significant bearish momentum.
“The mechanism matters here. It is not that people are swapping their gold for oil,” Said said. “Higher oil means higher inflation, higher inflation keeps central banks hawkish. On top of that, when the tech selloff hit, people sold gold to cover margin calls elsewhere. Gold is liquid, so it is the first thing that gets sold when people need cash. So in this war gold is not acting as the safe haven people expect. Oil and the dollar are taking that role.”
With all the attention on inflation and oil prices, Naeem Aslam, CIO of Zaye Capital Markets, said that next week's midterm elections could have an impact on the outlook.
Some political analysts have said that if Democrats regain control of Congress, winning majorities in both the House and Senate, it could become more difficult for the Trump administration to continue its war with Iran.
Analysts have said that anything that eases tensions in the Middle East and ends the global energy supply crunch could be positive for gold.
Aslam said he still expects any major dip in gold prices to represent a long-term buying opportunity.
Jeff Sarti, CEO of Morton Wealth, said that he also sees a buying opportunity for gold, as the latest selloff appears to be a technical move.
“DSI sentiment is flashing very bearish, which from a contrarian point of view indicates that this may be a strong entry point,” he said.
Sarti added that he is also not concerned about gold's broken correlation with bond yields over the past week.
“Much of the reason why yields are moderating is that there has been a sentiment shift away from the mega cap tech stocks into the safety net of bonds. But, the counter is that the latest GDP data was strong , implying that bond yields should be higher as opposed to lower. So, I think that there is some short-term noise, tied to stock market sentiment, pushing bond yields lower, as opposed to the assumption that the odds of interest rate hikes are moderating,” he said.
Looking ahead, investors will have plenty of potential catalysts to navigate as financial markets remain volatile. Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections could have significant implications for the ongoing conflict with Iran and the outlook for energy prices, while Friday's nonfarm payrolls report will provide an important update on the health of the U.S. labor market.
With gold struggling to attract safe-haven demand and inflation concerns keeping the Federal Reserve on a tightening path, analysts expect the precious metal to remain sensitive to shifting interest-rate expectations and broader market sentiment.

articles.title_orig: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Case, Avoiding Trial
articles.title_zh: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Case, Avoiding Trial
articles.content_orig:
Meta has settled a social media addiction lawsuit , resolving claims against the technology giant before the case was set to go to trial next month, according to a lawyer for one of the plaintiffs.
The suit was brought by an 18-year-old woman identified in court documents as K.D.B. who alleged that Meta and Snapchat parent company Snap, which remains a defendant in the case, designed their social media platforms to foster addictive behavior. Another plaintiff in the lawsuit, dubbed S.J., settled with Meta last week.
Terms of Meta's settlement were not disclosed.
S.J. and K.D.B. also originally sued TikTok and Alphabet's YouTube platform, which each separately settled before trial.
The plaintiffs claim that the social media platforms contributed to their mental health struggles.
A spokesperson for the Lanier Law Firm, which is representing the plaintiffs, said they will proceed with their complaint against Snap.
"Each plaintiff alleges that Snap designed Snapchat to maximize the time young users spend on the app, using features such as Snapstreaks, Snapscores, push notifications, and filters, and that their compulsive use of Snapchat caused and contributed to severe mental and physical health injuries, including depression, anxiety, an eating disorder, and self-harm," the spokesperson said.
Snap disputes the allegations and has defended the company's practices.
Jury selection began this week in Los Angeles, with opening statements expected to begin in early November. Lawyers for the plaintiffs have said they expect the trial to last into mid-December.
"We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, the trial counsel for K.D.B., said in a statement.
A spokesperson for Meta, which still faces similar litigation alleging that its social platforms harm users' mental health, said the company will continue to defend itself in court.
"Trials, dismissals and settlements are all common in the bellwether process, and this litigation is no exception," she said in a statement. "We will continue to defend ourselves in court, and we stand by our record. We've spent more than a decade building protections for teens, and our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general goes even further with strict time limits, no access at night, and no notifications during school hours."
In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion to dozens of states that alleged the company used its social platforms, including Facebook and Instagram, to hook young internet users while concealing the risks.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Deepening Tech Selloff Pushes Nasdaq Toward Its Worst Month in Over a Year
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Deepening Tech Selloff Pushes Nasdaq Toward Its Worst Month in Over a Year
articles.content_orig:
By HUGO DUNCAN, BUSINESS EDITOR
Updated: 14:42 EDT, 30 October 2026
A Halloween slump in technology stocks has fuelled fears of a market crash that would hammer the savings and pensions of millions of British families.
On a brutal session in trading rooms in New York, the tech-heavy Nasdaq index followed up Thursday’s 1.4 per cent slide with a drop of more than 3 per cent on Friday.
Analysts warned of ‘tech carnage’ with shares in US giants Amazon and Intel among the biggest losers following bleak results on Thursday night.
Intel shares tumbled nearly 30 per cent – wiping around £90billion off its value – while Amazon fell more than 3 per cent.
The latest sell-off came after Google owner Alphabet tumbled more than 12 per cent on Thursday night – wiping close to £400billion off its value.
The tech titan, one of the so-called Magnificent Seven, is now down 30 per cent since its peak in May while the Nasdaq is off 7.5 per cent - wiping £2.5trillion off its value.
Traders are braced for turmoil on dealing floors around the world
A host of US tech stocks, driven to record highs this year on a wave of AI mania, are now in so-called ‘bear market’ territory – meaning they are down more than 20 per cent from their peak. Some have halved in value.
The FTSE 100 index has held up in the face of the sell-off – at least for now – as it benefits from a lack of exposure to tech and AI.
London’s blue-chip index closed up 7.71 points to 10,729.78 on Friday despite the ructions on Wall Street.
But the tech slump is proving painful for millions of British investors who are exposed to the US stock market through their pensions and Isas.
A host of Britain’s most popular investments, from technology funds and trusts and those that track major global indices, are packed full of US stocks now in reverse.
Neil Wilson, investor strategist at Saxo, warned of ‘tech carnage as October wraps up’ as investors fret over whether huge spending on AI infrastructure such as data centres will pay off.
He said: ‘This is starting to look quite ugly. The selloff looks a bit indiscriminate and shows that investors don't just want capex, they want to see the returns already.’
The AI trade has run into turbulence recently as investors grew uneasy about the billions Big Tech has poured into scaling up AI infrastructure while awaiting evidence of stronger returns.
Several companies have tapped the bond market to finance those investments, amplifying concerns that debt-funded spending will become harder to justify as borrowing costs rise.
Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said the slump in share prices in recent days ‘is a good example of how the AI trade has changed’.
He added: ‘At this point, the market isn't just asking how fast you can grow. It's asking what you have to spend to get there.’
The AI trade got a brief respite earlier this week when AI lab Anthropic – which is behind the Claude model – unveiled plans to list on the US stock market with a value of up to £1.5trillion.
Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said: ‘The FTSE 100’s lack of tech exposure has proved to be a blessing in disguise. The UK index is standing tall amid a global tech sell-off.'
Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, described the slump in New York as an 'AI reality check'.
He said: ‘Investors are increasingly unhappy at the huge sums of money being spent on AI infrastructure without a clear roadmap for when, or whether, those investments will deliver a sufficient return. That means investors are questioning if money is being spent wisely.
'Big tech companies are going all-in with their bets that AI will be the biggest thing in decades to transform business and consumer life. If they get that bet wrong, the fallout could be huge.'
He added: 'Tech stocks have gone from being investors’ main feast to stale bread.
'For years, investors have treated tech as the golden ticket to wealth creation, and for a long time they have been richly rewarded. That enthusiasm is now evaporating, and some investors are racing for the exit.
'The gigantic declines we’ve seen this week in shares such as Alphabet and Intel suggest that investor sentiment has been turned on its head. Current price action implies tech investors want to jump off the treadmill rather than slow it down.'
The top ten holdings of the highly popular Vanguard FTSE All World ET highlight how much big US tech shares matter to UK investors
Millions of British savers are exposed to US tech stocks – even if they don’t know it.
Companies such as Nvidia, Alphabet, Apple, Meta, Amazon and Intel are held in countless global funds that form the backbone of pension savings.
When these stocks go south, so can the value of the nest eggs held by workers and pensioners alike.
Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said: ‘The tech sell-off matters to investors around the world as the AI theme has weaved its way into countless sectors and geographies.
‘In particular, the US stock market is home to the giant tech names and is a major component of global funds that fill so many people’s investment portfolios.
‘This means that investors might find they have big tech exposure without realising it.’
He points out that 15 years ago, the US represented half of the MSCI World benchmark for the global stock market. It now stands at 73 per cent.
Tech is the dominant sector, making up more than 30 per cent of the index.
‘If tech goes off the boil, global funds might not provide the diversification support some investors expect,’ said Coatsworth.
For those who want to ‘dial down tech exposure’, he suggested switching into a global equity fund that excludes the US.
He pointed investors towards the iShares MSCI World ex-US ETF, which invests in a basket of companies from around the world excluding the US.
Tech stocks only account for 10.9 per cent of the portfolio, with financials the dominant sector at 27.9 per cent and industrials at 17.6 per cent.
‘The main holdings include banks, healthcare companies, oil producers and miners,’ said Coatsworth.
‘That would provide more sector balance and less dependence on tech, but it would mean some of the key names that have led the US market rally in recent years like Nvidia no longer being in the driving seat.’

articles.title_orig: Traffic Control Errors Caused Spain’s Deadly Train Crash, Official Says
articles.title_zh: Traffic Control Errors Caused Spain’s Deadly Train Crash, Official Says
articles.content_orig:
An Oklahoma City arts leader is missing after a deadly high-speed train crash in Spain that injured his husband and killed dozens of people.
Fernando Calvillo, 45, community relations director of the Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition, was last seen aboard a train traveling along the Madrid-Seville line when two high-speed trains collided Wednesday in one of the country's deadliest railway disasters in decades.
Calvillo was travelling with his husband, Lawrence Naff, who is hospitalized and recovering from his injuries.
Members of the OKC arts community close to the couple described Naff and Calvillo as "wonderful people who have given so much to the arts community."
"It's hard that we can't do anything at this time to help them because they would be the first ones to help someone else," said Danielle Ezell, the Interim Executive Director of Oklahomans for the Arts.
Family members from both parties have traveled to Spain to assist the embassy and the civil guard in search efforts, as well as provide support to Naff's recovery.
The train crash is Spain's worst since 2013, and has killed 69 so far, injuring dozens more. This is the second major crash on the Madrid-Seville line this year.
Three days of national mourning have been declared in the country.
"If anyone who was traveling on that train, any volunteer, emergency responder, rescue worker, or hospital staff member saw Fernando, helped him, or remembers even the smallest detail, we ask from the bottom of our hearts that you please share that information," a statement from a family representative said.
"We also ask for your help in sharing his photograph. You may not have any information yourself, but sharing his picture could help us reach someone who does. As a family, we continue to hold on to hope that we will hear news about Fernando very soon. All we want is to find him. Any information, no matter how small, could make a difference."
The family asks if anyone has information about Calvillo or his whereabouts to contact local authorities at +52-449-222-8649 or +1 (405) 836-2880.

articles.title_orig: Tomb Raider (Game Boy) - 'The Editors Had to Retcon the Score Because It Was Higher than Pokémon and Zelda'
articles.title_zh: Tomb Raider (Game Boy) - 'The Editors Had to Retcon the Score Because It Was Higher than Pokémon and Zelda'
articles.content_orig:
This month sees the launch of the Making of Tomb Raider 1997-2000 book, an unofficial deep-dive into the creation of some of Lara Croft's most beloved adventures, written by me, Daryl Baxter .
In case you're keen for a taster of what the book might contain, I've included an excerpt which focuses on Lara's Nintendo debut, which took place on the Game Boy Color in 2000.
At this point, I'll hand over the mic to artist Matt Charlesworth , who was kind enough to speak with me about the creation of this beloved handheld title.
"After helping with Tomb Raider 3 via the loading screens, I got chatting with Sean Dunlevy , who had just finished working on Fighting Force 64 . We were both super excited about working on the newly released Game Boy Color, as it gave him a chance to get back to low-level ASM coding on simpler 8-bit systems, and it allowed me to learn an art form that was (at that time) dead on major home consoles and game systems: pixel art.
After a month or two of prototyping, Sean and I had the framework of a cartoony space adventure with similar gameplay to Flashback / Another World , called Salvage . It was at this point that we realised that we could make this into a pretty great portable TR game, so we met with [Core Design boss] Jeremy Smith and got the approval to do exactly that.
Sean and I started on that project for different reasons. I think he wanted to avoid the larger team sizes and codebase of the PS1 generation, and I wanted to have a place where I could rapidly learn new techniques to broaden my skill set without the stress and focus drawn by working on the flagship PS1 games. Sean was a seasoned veteran programmer by this time, and as I stated before, I knew very little but was eager to learn.
Teaming up with Sean was a great experience, and I’m lucky I had that experience with him in particular, as he was patient and great at explaining the technical things I needed to understand without ever patronising or talking down to me. I’m extremely grateful to him for that time.
Lightning then struck twice when we hired gameplay programmer Ian Manders from Rare – another incredible person who was a joy to work with. Despite being closer to my age than Sean, he brought with him a ton of experience from Rare, having shipped Donkey Kong Country games on Game Boy and Ken Griffey Jr.’s Winning Run on the Super Nintendo console.
Tomb Raider felt like a direct 3D evolution of games such as Prince Of Persia , Another World, and Flashback, so it seemed obvious to us that a 2D TR game should evoke similar mechanics and gameplay to feel authentic and on brand.
We made progress pretty quickly on the game, but it also became obvious really fast that I wouldn’t be able to do all of the art myself for the entire game – it was too much and I had too much to learn. I don’t remember exactly how it happened, but thankfully, at just the right time, a bunch of animation grads from Ballyfermot Animation College in Ireland arrived at Core, and we were able to pick Fergus [Duggan] and Paschal [McGuire] to add to our team.
Although Paschal struggled a little to transition into game development, Fergus was the right person we needed. He took on and owned the entire background art for the game and allowed me to focus on Lara and enemy art, and animation. He did an unbelievable job, and I think his work on both Game Boy games stands up to this day.
At the outset, I remember the legendary Jerr O’Carroll also assisting me with learning 2D pixel art and design as we explored the Salvage project, but he didn’t transition with us onto the Tomb Raider game, as I think he was animating on TR4 as far as I remember. But shortly after Fergus and Paschal joined us, Lee Pullen (whose pixel art defined the characters of the Chuck Rock series) also lent a hand and taught me a bunch about efficiently conveying motion with the extreme constraints of super low-res pixel art.
The thing I remember most from that time was working incredibly long hours and feeling way out of my depth, but having my late friend Troy Horton producing our game made it manageable, and thanks to him, we knew everything would be alright.
After probably about a year, we were done, and THQ published the game. We shipped that after about a year of incredibly hard work and crazy hours (all self-inflicted) and received at least one 10/10 review from a GB-specific print magazine at the time. It’s hilarious, but looking through that archive, I see that the editors of the magazine had to retcon the review score down after several issues because it was ranking higher than Pokémon and Zelda !
This was an incredibly rewarding game to work on, especially as it was my first real game I contributed to in a truly meaningful way, and because Sean and I ran the project and had full creative control."

articles.title_orig: We Must Kill Windows For A Just Future
articles.title_zh: We Must Kill Windows For A Just Future
articles.content_orig:
Nobody likes Windows. This cannot continue. We must come together and annihilate it. I hate to say it, but the way forward is Linux
You never use Windows because you like Windows–you use Windows because it is there. This has been true my entire life. I have lived through the operating system’s ups and downs, including Windows Millennium Edition, which was worse than you could imagine and, somehow, worse than its reputation. But while Windows 10 was sorta okay, Windows 11 is wretched. The day-to-day experience of using it has deteriorated into something dreadful. If we continue to enable Microsoft, the walls will decay and fester eternally. We must escape this cycle of pain together.
Microsoft as a company, minus many of the good gaming companies it bought and the employees at the margins allowed to make tiny useful pieces of software, is a rot plaguing the world. Be it its active aiding in the genocide in Gaza , its unhinged commitment to AI , or just the fact that Windows and the 365 Suite have always sucked a little to use, the compromise that has existed with regular people for a long time has disintegrated. To the extent that computing can be moral, a moral future must be one without Microsoft generally and Windows specifically. We cannot assume that Windows will collapse under its own mediocrity; if that were true it would have happened decades ago. We must kill Windows. We must cut it out from our lives like a tumor; we must systematically consider what we need from it and seek to construct alternatives with purpose. It turns out that’s still quite hard, but every single day the process is easier.
For clarity and as a point of policy, it is worth mentioning that while Xbox is the subject of a “priority boycott” by BDS, Microsoft generally is categorized as a “pressure target. ” These are slightly different asks, as the BDS movement itself acknowledges how difficult it is to divorce oneself from Microsoft either personally or vocationally, asking on its website to “consider switching [to] free and open software instead of another, possibly complicit company.” This is in part due to the insidious, rent-seeking nature of Microsoft that has wormed its way into the fabric of everyday life: It is easier to cancel your Game Pass account than it is to tell your boss you’re not using Teams or to install Linux Mint on a company laptop. It is not a personal failing to be required to use Windows for your job.
Aftermath reached out to BDS, who provided us with the following statement about the boycott. Here it is in full.
But it is not just BDS making the call for alternatives, as many people outside of the United States understand that the hegemonic nature of US tech is itself a liability to everyone in the world. (My colleague Tech Won’t Save Us podcaster and author Paris Marx has written a guide about this that I quite like.) As the United States becomes increasingly erratic, other countries are realizing that they need an offramp. France’s Interministerial Directorate for Digital Affairs (DINUM) recently announced that they are in the process of transitioning to a version of NixOS called SécurixOS and are working to formulate a long term plan. "The State can no longer simply acknowledge its dependence; it must break free,” David Amiel, France’s minister of public action, said in a statement in April. “We must become less reliant on American tools and regain control of our digital destiny." Similarly, the Dutch government is also developing its own variant of NixOS called Digitaal Autonome Werkomgeving Overheid or Digital Automated Working Environment (DAWO ).
“The world has now seen very clearly how the US government and the billionaires of Silicon Valley will work together to wield the dependence of countries around the world on the US cloud, digital services, and social media platforms against them — even going so far as to completely cut off members of the International Criminal Court, the United Nations, and former European Union officials,” Paris Marx told me via direct message. “US tech companies and their government can no longer be trusted, and that makes dependence on US tech an inherent threat to sovereignty — not to mention the existing threats to a healthy society that have been accumulating for years. As long as that dependence continues, the United States can use it as a weapon.”
If complicity in a ongoing genocide was not enough, Microsoft has hitched its future on artificial intelligence. It is a move that is an existential risk to the economy, a security risk, and somehow the most annoying thing the company has ever done with its OS in its entire history. Microsoft is a key part of the cadre of useless jackasses making the computer expensive . Though Windows 11 had some nice additions at the beginning (Powertoys, Winget , the sound design), the experience itself has become garbage as they have shoved more and more half-broken shit into the operating system. Basically no person on Earth wanted the controversial Recall feature that took snapshots of your computer . Copilot is a nightmare that nobody seriously uses on an OS level, and Microsoft has said their goal long term is to get people “addicted” to their AI assistants . Microsoft’s very conception of what they envision the operating system becoming, an “ agentic OS ” is glassy-eyed, tech sector cult pablum masquerading as visionary and a direction I am fundamentally opposed to for a machine that I use to play Balatro and answer emails.
Every mandatory update to Windows 11 is a slot machine that might make your computer run like a dog that ate a bag of dark chocolate. It has gotten so bad that Microsoft’s chief of Windows Pavan Davuluri had to write a we-acknowledge-this-OS-sucks-ass blog to address how unusable and intrusive the entire rats nest has become, and made a commitment to do better . Not to call the man a liar, but I am going to tell you, as someone who had to interact with Windows for decades, that in the long run that isn’t going to happen. If you believe that even a little bit you are a rube and should consider your life choices.
There is a black hole at the heart of that company, and no minor gains that Windows claws back will ever make up for the inescapable gravity of Microsoft products getting shittier over time. They will extract rent from you and your employer at every plausible juncture and give you garbage in exchange. You must accept in your heart that Windows is a lost cause. Once you do, the work begins.
Around 2010 I remember waiting in line to get into PAX East and being approached by a guy handing out burned CDs. He was distributing copies of Linux, either Mandrake or Red Hat, to everyone waiting in line. Had I heard the good word? I had. I have tried many times before to divorce myself from Windows over the years, each time with varying success. I have existed between hardcore PC building and being a Mac person my entire life — a status that remains to this day in the hodgepodge of devices in my office.
From a purely conceptual perspective, the well-meaning dweeb handing out burned software in line has been vindicated. The arc of history is long and bends towards open source software. I should be clear that Linux is not morally good on its own; it can and often is used for evil ends. Linux has the same slop problem every other piece of software has, and Linus Torvalds needs an intervention over AI coding . But Linux is also free, and not simply in the monetary sense of the word.
I had tried installing Linux on my home PC back in the 2000s, but it didn’t stick the second I realized I couldn’t play Final Fantasy XI on it. I have lived on and off with elements of Linux in my life — multiple network devices I own run some variant of Debian Linux, I regularly had WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) enabled, and I have often put my machine in dual boot for specific use cases. I have two Macs and a PC at my desk and use the same unified shell for both. My choice

articles.title_orig: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.title_zh: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.content_orig:
European diplomats have refused to stand for an official photo with Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov at the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in the US, leading to the American hosts cancelling the planned picture.
Two officials confirmed to the BBC the cancellation of the so-called family photo scheduled for Friday morning, which would usually include representatives from all the nations in attendance.
The meeting, which gathers top diplomats from the world's biggest economies, is being hosted in Atlanta by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Ukraine is not not a G20 member but has been invited to similar meetings in recent years. However, Ukraine was not invited to this meeting.
Relations between Ukraine and the US have been particularly tense this month, with a diplomatic standoff between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump over Kyiv's strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is present and a diplomatic source confirmed the UK was among the countries which refused to participate in the picture.
One British official said: "The UK has a longstanding policy not to have direct, bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion of Ukraine and we are not about to change that".
A US official said the photo was cancelled "after it became clear some of the delegations were unwilling to participate in a joint photo".
"Rather than allow a ceremonial photo opportunity to become a diplomatic distraction, the US decided to forgo the photo and keep the focus on the substantive discussions," the official said.
In contrast to Ukraine, relations between the US and Russia appear to have partially thawed in recent weeks, as Trump waived some sanctions and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the American market.
The move comes as Trump attempts to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of mid-term elections at the start of November, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.
Ukraine and its European allies have heavily criticised Trump's deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Zelensky called it "a gift" to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".
Trump said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Putin has said Russia, which introduced a ban on diesel exports earlier this year, is willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and currently controls approximately a fifth of Ukrainian territory.
Moscow has in recent weeks intensified its deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.
