articles.title_orig: FCC Plans Vote To Block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom From U.S. Phone Numbers
articles.title_zh: FCC Plans Vote To Block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom From U.S. Phone Numbers
articles.content_orig:
Published 30 Oct 2026, 17:24 UTC
This article is an automated aggregation of coverage from news outlets. Our editorials offer in-depth analysis curated by the NewsCord team.
FCC to vote November 19 blocking Chinese telcos' direct access to US numbers Policy targets China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other IP-enabled service providers
The United States Federal Communications Commission plans to vote on November 19 on a proposal to block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other internet-based service providers from direct access to American phone numbers. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said, "With this decision, the FCC will be strengthening our first line of defense against bad actors and illegal robocallers," as the proposal targets Voice over Internet Protocol technology that converts voice into digital data and transmits it over broadband connections. The FCC framed the restrictions as a national security measure aimed at preventing scam-related robocalls, and the proposal would also cover IP-enabled service providers that obtain U.S. numbers through internet-based voice services.
The FCC also announced plans to prohibit IP-enabled service providers from using equipment manufactured by companies on its list of entities considered national security risks, including Huawei and ZTE. The FCC said it would ban all Chinese laboratories from testing US electronics in December 2028, and it is considering revoking direct phone number authorisations for Chinese companies it considers security risks.
China’s foreign ministry said it firmly opposed the proposed restrictions, accusing Washington of abusing national security concerns to suppress Chinese companies. Guo Jiakun told a daily press conference, "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests," as the FCC moved to tighten rules around Chinese telecom access. The FCC also said it plans to bar IP-enabled service providers that use equipment from companies on the FCC's list that pose national security risks, including Huawei or ZTE.
The FCC added that it would ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics in December 2028 and may also revoke direct number authorizations for Chinese companies that it deems to pose a national security risk. The FCC has previously prohibited China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, and it is considering additional measures including blocking connections to US networks and operating data centres in the country.
Washington’s concerns about potential espionage and other security threats linked to Chinese access to American telecommunications infrastructure have grown in recent years, with the FCC tying the curbs to national security and robocall prevention. In late 2024, the US government said a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group known as Salt Typhoon had stolen consumers’ call records and US call data while infiltrating telecommunications companies and infrastructure. The FBI said this year that threats from Salt Typhoon were "still very much ongoing," as the FCC’s proposal advanced toward its November 19 vote.
The FCC also added California-based Digitalsystem Technology to its list of companies considered national security risks in July, citing links to Chinese telecommunications firms and its ownership by a Chinese national. The FCC’s broader package includes barring Chinese laboratories from testing US electronics in December 2028 and considering whether to revoke direct access authorisations, while the Chinese government has consistently denied wrongdoing.

articles.title_orig: Samsung Mocks iPhone Duo Display Cracks in New Ad Campaign
articles.title_zh: Samsung Mocks iPhone Duo Display Cracks in New Ad Campaign
articles.content_orig:
Samsung has released a new Instagram ad that subtly humiliates Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo .
The ad shows a green apple cut in half and tries—but ultimately fails—to fold the two pieces together, implying the apple will snap if it goes any further. Samsung then shows the Galaxy Z Fold 8 as a smoother alternative and ends the video by pointing out that it is "Years ahead in Foldables."
With what's been happening with the iPhone Duo lately, the ad couldn't be any more apt. Many early buyers and testers have reported cracked or dead-pixel-lined inner displays and hinge-related problems within hours or days of unboxing. While the issue is thought to affect only a small percentage of iPhone Duos sold, it's widespread enough to have been dubbed "Crackgate."
Beyond using its ad to throw shade at the Duo, Samsung shows off concrete differences between its book-style foldable and Apple's. The ad notes that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 measures 9.7mm when folded and weighs 201g, while the iPhone Duo measures 11.3mm and weighs 254g.
Unfortunately for Apple, Samsung's "years ahead" claim is a simple fact: It launched the original Galaxy Fold in 2019, while Apple entered the foldable market just this month. Samsung is currently on its 8th generation of foldables. Apple fans have long defended the brand's slower pace by saying it takes what Android phones have already done and improves upon that technology, but this ad is going to be a tough one for Apple to answer.

articles.title_orig: Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
articles.title_zh: Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
articles.content_orig:
RJ Scaringe spent nearly half of Rivian’s earnings call hyping self-driving tech. But taking on Tesla’s FSD with custom chips and pricey lidar is an enormous gamble while the mass-market R2 is still scaling up.
RJ Scaringe spent nearly half of Rivian’s earnings call hyping self-driving tech. But taking on Tesla’s FSD with custom chips and pricey lidar is an enormous gamble while the mass-market R2 is still scaling up.
During an hourlong earnings call last night , Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe spent less time talking about the production ramp of the all-important R2 SUV than he did hyping the company’s still-unproven autonomous vehicle ambitions .
But the company faces a crucial test later this year, when it rolls out its point-to-point hands-free driving feature — first to its own employees for testing and validation in 2026, and later to customers in 2027. Following that, Rivian says it will launch its first robotaxi vehicles in partnership with Uber in 2028 . In short, the next two years will determine whether Rivian will succeed or fail in its high-stakes quest to become a full-stack autonomy player.
“We believe autonomy is a primary product differentiator, market share driver, and long-term value creator,” Derek Mulvey, VP for finance, said during the call.
Success is not guaranteed. Tesla has a huge head start with its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) in over 1.7 million active customer cars. But trying to match Tesla’s driver-assist features — while simultaneously designing its own silicon chips , buying pricey sensors, and paying for massive AI computing power — is a huge financial gamble, especially while Rivian is still struggling to build and sell its mass-market R2 vehicles at scale. (The R2 recently became Rivian’s best-selling vehicle by volume, so progress continues.)
“We believe autonomy is a primary product differentiator, market share driver, and long-term value creator.”
But it’s unclear whether Rivian sees the R2 as its make-or-break vehicle or if solving autonomy will be the true decider. That leaves the company in the middle of a difficult balancing act: launching an ambitious, mass-market electric vehicle while simultaneously reinventing itself as a full-stack autonomous driving powerhouse.
Of course, the feature itself needs to work for Rivian to succeed. During the call, Scaringe revealed that he has been using the new point-to-point driving system in his own commute to the office every day, calling it “a wonderful” experience. He continued:
So, our view is that that is going to become a big driver of demand. And I think it’s unclear how quickly the whole — you know, the whole US market and the whole automotive market — starts to shift to really wanting this, and this being a major purchase criterion. But certainly, we’re at the front end of an inflection point where it’s more and more people exposed to what this could do… We do think it’s a really big driver, in the long term, for market share for us.
But Scaringe was cagey about other details. When asked about Rivian’s take rate for its Autonomy Plus package — in other words, what percentage of Rivian buyers who purchase or subscribe to the software out of the total customer base — the chief executive declined to share the exact number. “The take rate on Autonomy Plus has exceeded our expectations,” he said, “and we’re quite encouraged by it.”
Rivian’s execs are no doubt envious of Tesla’s take rates for FSD: Over 75 percent of new Tesla buyers in North America opted to get FSD in the third quarter of 2026 , the company recently reported. Meanwhile, Rivian reported $605 million in revenue from software and subscription services in Q3 2026, a 45 percent increase year over year. And Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin.
Rivian will likely spend more money than it brings in as it keeps buying expensive computers and AI systems. On the call, the company pointed out that computer chips, memory, and electronics are getting pricier. It also warned that adding two processors and costly lidar sensors to some R2 models could eat into the profits it hoped to make by building the vehicle in large numbers.
The point-to-point system will face its own hurdles, including edge cases and the complexities of urban driving. A vehicle crash could damage Rivian’s brand and reputation, just as Tesla has experienced many times with FSD . And even though Rivian intends to roll out the feature to require active driver supervision, the company will likely face legal challenges when things inevitably go wrong.
To be sure, Rivian couldn’t afford to sit on the sidelines and concede the autonomous crown to Tesla and Waymo. Self-driving tech could help Rivian post big, software-company-style profits, but paying for expensive AI development while also trying to build the R2 at scale makes the next year or two its riskiest period ever.

articles.title_orig: EU diplomats object to G20 photo with Lavrov, prompting US cancellation
articles.title_zh: EU diplomats object to G20 photo with Lavrov, prompting US cancellation
articles.content_orig:
The United States cancelled a planned group photo of foreign ministers from the world's 20 largest economies (G20) on Friday after several European diplomats objected to being photographed alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to walk out.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio decided to cancel the photo to avoid further controversy, according to two US officials who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the matter.
Opening the talks, Rubio looked ahead, saying he hoped for “a productive meeting.”
“We are in a critical moment — I would call it a moment of choosing, and I would say not just for my country, the United States of America, but frankly, for the world," he said.
“We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises,” he added, many posing "severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”
The cancellation of the traditional group photo highlighted tensions within the G20, as diplomats face difficult negotiations over the war in Ukraine, the US-Israeli war against Iran, US tariffs and disputes in the South China Sea.
Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said the cancellation of the group photo was “the right decision” by the US, telling media in Atlanta that “I am not the only one who does not want to be photographed with Lavrov.”
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said “there is no normality with Russia” but “we must exchange the controversies at the table here,” the German news agency dpa reported. He added that “we also must not send falsely optimistic signals.”
Even before the dispute over the photo, several G20 countries had raised concerns about Russia's invitation amid intensified attacks on Ukraine.
Tensions have also grown after Trump waived new sanctions on Moscow and temporarily restricted logistical and intelligence support for Kyiv, further straining US-Ukraine relations.

articles.title_orig: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
articles.title_zh: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
articles.content_orig:
The Project Suncatcher satellite generated a haiku about being in space.
The Project Suncatcher satellite generated a haiku about being in space.
Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month .
“Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.”

Asian trading is mixed as worries about the future of artificial intelligence grow after Alphabet’s stock drop dragged on U.S. markets
TOKYO -- Asian shares were trading mixed Friday, as worries about the future of artificial intelligence grew after Alphabet's stock drop dragged on U.S. markets.
Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 dropped 2.3% in afternoon trading to 63,155.94. At the end of its two-day monetary policy board meeting, the Bank of Japan decided to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%. That was widely expected because the central bank raised the rate last month.
The U.S. has been pressuring Japan to raise rates because of concerns about the weakening yen. In currency trading, the U.S. dollar inched up to 157.67 Japanese yen from 157.65 yen. The euro cost $1.1186, up from $1.1181.
Australia's S & P/ASX 200 rose 0.2% to 8,908.10. South Korea's Kospi declined nearly 4% to 5,701.71, as shares in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics both slipped.
Shares related to the great market interest in AI have tended to be volatile, because some issues, including chip makers, get pushed up because of that interest, but then may decline because of worries about supplies, for instance.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng added 1.7% to 23,359.06, while the Shanghai Composite lost 0.4% to 3,636.60.
On Wall Street, the S & P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days , even though the wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132 points, or 0.3%.
Alphabet is one of the most influential stocks on Wall Street because it’s one of the largest, and the Class A shares of its stock fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago.
All told, the S & P 500 fell 23.59 points to 7,720.39 Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132.54 to 52,342.56, and the Nasdaq composite tumbled 365.13 to 26,184.72.
In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.94% from 5.05% late Wednesday. It’s been generally pulling back since it topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.
In energy trading, benchmark U.S. crude gained 1.15% to $103.17 a barrel. Brent crude, the international standard, edged up 1.05% to $116.09 a barrel.

Oops, something went wrong
By Sinéad Carew and Iain Withers
NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - A sharp selloff in Wall Street's tech shares pushed MSCI's global index down 1.5% on Friday, sending investors to the safety of US bonds on fears that hefty cash-burning AI investments may not deliver sufficient returns.
Shares in chipmaker Intel < INTC.O> plunged 28.6% ‌and Amazon shares lost 1.4% after their results each showed that they burned through cash while investing heavily in AI-related development. Intel also said PC demand had slowed, ‌and that it could persist through next year.
Shares in Google parent Alphabet lost another 1.4%, having slid 12.6% on Thursday, after it reported that massive AI spending turned the company's cash flow negative.
"We've had such a huge move up ​in the whole complex," said Sahak Manuelian, managing director for global equities sales and trading at Wedbush Securities, referring to AI-related stocks. "When you've had the parabolic-like moves, it makes for a very nasty downdraft. I think that's what we're seeing. And then you have people that are starting to pull money out and going to other areas."
Earlier, Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, described Friday's stock trading as a "horror show" with AI spending being the villain as cash burn and elevated capex prompted questions about whether the AI returns will "justify the outlays."
Goldman also said pressure from rising ‌oil prices due to more attacks in the Middle East ⁠and concerns about a hack at Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, added to the gloom. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies fell.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 572.25 points, or 1.09%, to 51,770.31, the S&P 500 fell 140.32 points, or 1.82%, to 7,580.07 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 747.73 points, ⁠or 2.86%, to 25,437.00.
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 17.15 points, or 1.51%, to 1,115.47. Earlier, the pan-European STOXX 600 index finished down 0.36%.
On Wall Street, Intel's selloff spread across the chip sector. The PHLX semiconductor index finished down more than 7% after touching its lowest level since May, marking its biggest daily drop since late June. The S&P 500 technology index lost 4.2% in its ​weakest ​day since early June.
Investors looking for safer bets pushed up consumer staples and utilities. But the top performer ​on the day was energy, which was bolstered by oil's rally ‌and results from Exxon Mobil and Chevron. The oil majors posted strong profits due to big refining margins driven by supply disruptions from Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and the Iran war.
In currencies, the yen was headed for its third consecutive daily gain against the dollar on Friday after the Bank of Japan held rates steady but revised up its inflation forecast, while a fresh wave of selling in AI shares triggered demand for non-dollar safe havens.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.04% to 101.92, with the euro down 0.13% at $1.1163.
Against the Japanese yen, the dollar weakened 0.1% to 157.54.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 2.49% to $76,877.30. Ethereum declined 1.01% to $2,236.76.
US Treasuries rose and the benchmark 10-year ‌yield was eyeing its biggest monthly drop in nearly three years as the selloff in technology-related stocks ​pushed investors into the safe-haven asset.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 5.8 basis points to 4.931% ​while the 30-year bond yield fell 1.97 basis points to 5.3093%.
The 2-year note yield, ​which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 6.64 basis points to 4.59%.
Oil prices settled at six-month highs ‌as traders braced for a potential escalation in the Iran war after ​the US midterm elections on Tuesday. The war ​has lingered for eight months without a resolution. On Friday, a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked, highlighting the ongoing supply risks. [O/R]
US crude settled up 2.08%, or $2.12, to $104.12 a barrel. Brent finished at $117.63 per barrel, up 2.4%, or $2.76 a barrel, on the day.
Precious metals fell. Gold dropped to a one-year low on Friday and ​silver slid below $50 an ounce for the first time since November ‌2025, as higher energy prices and persistent inflation concerns strengthened expectations that US interest rates will stay high.
Spot gold fell 3.63% to $3,874.58 an ounce and spot ​silver fell 6.36% to $49.06 an ounce.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia denies report that its CEO was allegedly targeted in Chinese spy plot
articles.title_zh: Nvidia denies report that its CEO was allegedly targeted in Chinese spy plot
articles.content_orig:
The report claimed the CEO was targeted by an executive at Megaspeed.
Nvidia, a top chipmaker, is denying a report that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was allegedly targeted in a Chinese spy plot.
According to a New York Times report published Thursday, U.S. intelligence officials allegedly determined that a top executive at a Singapore-based data center company who developed a "close relationship" with Huang was funneling information to Chinese officials in Beijing.
The executive was identified by the Times as Alice Huang, who was pictured together with the Nvidia CEO in 2024.
Nvidia denied the report in a statement to ABC News, saying Jensen Huang "talks with thousands of customer executives every year."
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected," the statement read. "Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job."
A spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry also denied the report.
“The reports are baseless and purely slanderous smears against China,” spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Friday at his daily press briefing.
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment.
According to the Times, President Donald Trump was briefed on U.S. intelligence officials' findings but did not take any action.
The White House has not yet responded to ABC News' request for comment.
Trump is a close ally of Jensen Huang, who has advised the president amid an artificial intelligence race with China. Jensen Huang was a guest at a White House state dinner in September, where Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping.
That same month, the CEO attended a luncheon for AI and tech industry leaders hosted by Trump at the White House.
Earlier this year, in January, Huang convinced the president to clear the way for advance chip sales to China, in a deal that gave the U.S. government 25% of the profits.
Trump also personally owns shares in Nvidia, the world's most publicly traded company.

articles.title_orig: FDA again bypasses advisers to remove black-box warnings from menopause treatments
articles.title_zh: FDA again bypasses advisers to remove black-box warnings from menopause treatments
articles.content_orig:
Some experts express concern about ‘lack of transparency’ as agency removes warnings on three estrogen patches
Three more patches for treating menopause will no longer carry black-box warnings about cardiovascular disease, breast cancer and dementia, officials at the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) said on Friday.
The FDA did not convene an advisory committee and offered few details on the scientific basis for the decision in the press briefing. The news follows the removal of black-box warnings from six menopause treatments in February, as patients across the US struggle with shortages of the patches.
When journalists asked for the evidence behind this decision, officials said it could be provided later.
“I have been concerned by the lack of transparency behind these decisions,” said Reshma Ramachandran, an assistant professor and health services researcher at Yale School of Medicine. “The blanket removal of black-box warnings regarding risks of breast cancer and cardiovascular disease without clear justification can be misleading for patients and underplays real potential harms.”
There are particular risks for certain groups of patients, such as those with histories of hormone-sensitive cancers, she said. Instead, officials highlighted the shortages patients are facing for menopause hormone treatments (MHT).
“We are working with manufacturers to strengthen supply and improve access,” said Dorothy Fink, deputy director of the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development. Manufacturing of estrogen patches has doubled over the past year, she said.
Even so, patients report stock-outs of the patches.
“We know that for some patients, these past months have been frustrating,” said Sarah Ibrahim, deputy center director for regulatory programs of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. After the change to labels in February, demand for estradiol patches “increased significantly, and patients in many areas found it difficult to get their usual patches at their usual pharmacy”, she said. “And I want you to know that we hear you.”
The FDA is working with manufacturers to ramp up production, and the agency is also working to change the labels of the remaining MHT products, Ibrahim said.
The black-box warnings “painted a broad and, in some cases, overstated pictures of risk”, she said. “Updated evidence shows that for many healthy women under 60 and within 10 years of menopause onset, the risk-benefit profile looks meaningfully different than older warnings conveyed.”
Estradiol patches are usually considered lower risk than synthetic oral medications, because they pass into the bloodstream without first going to the liver. The risks of the patches are higher with high doses, research shows .
Officials in the Trump administration have made sweeping and “ data-free ” claims about the benefits of MHT, including improvements in longevity, which are not supported by research, menopause experts have said. While there are benefits to the treatments for some women, the decision not to convene advisers or include research sets a troubling precedent, they said.
The FDA bypassed its advisory committees last November in announcing it would remove the warnings; at the time, a spokesperson said that the reason is because committees are “bureaucratic, long, often conflicted, and very expensive”.
Instead, the FDA convened a panel in July 2025 featuring doctors and influencers, all of whom were vocal proponents of MHT and several of whom had conflicts of interest with practices that market and sell hormone therapy, Ramachandran said.
“At the expert meeting, they also did not allow for public testimony,” Ramachandran said – including from the lead investigator of the Women’s Health Initiative, research from which formed the recommendations for MHT, who was in the audience. After audience members voiced concern, the FDA opened a docket for public comment.
The FDA is also exploring the possibility of offering vaginal estrogen products over the counter, according to an agency press release on Friday.

Julianne Geiger is a veteran energy journalist and market analyst with more than a decade of experience covering the global oil and gas sector. Her…
ExxonMobil reported $15.4 billion in third-quarter profit Friday, more than double its earnings a year earlier, with its Gulf Coast refineries running at full capacity and diesel prices doing the rest.
The company earned $3.72 per share, or $4.23 on an adjusted basis, beating Wall Street's $4.08 estimate. Adjusted net income reached $17.5 billion, making it one of Exxon's most profitable quarters ever.
Exxon's energy products business earned $9.05 billion in adjusted profit, up from $4.1 billion in the second quarter. Its U.S. Gulf Coast refinery units operated at 100% utilization, producing their second-highest diesel volumes on record.
The Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have sidelined roughly 10% of global refining capacity, leaving the remaining plants to supply a market desperately short of diesel and other fuels. Refining margins have soared, and Exxon is certainly making the most of them.
The company has also increased the amount of fuel it can produce. Its Gulf Coast distillate output is up approximately 40% since 2019, helped by the $2 billion Beaumont refinery expansion completed in 2023. That project added 250,000 barrels per day of processing capacity, an investment approved years before today's fuel shortage.
Exxon's upstream business had a less impressive quarter. Adjusted earnings fell to $7.3 billion from $9.2 billion in the second quarter as crude prices eased. Production held near 4.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Exxon generated $25.7 billion in operating cash flow and returned $9.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and stock repurchases, including $5.1 billion in buybacks. It also increased its dividend for the 44th consecutive year and announced plans for another $20 billion in share repurchases in 2027.
With Exxon's Gulf Coast refineries already operating at full capacity, further production increases will be difficult without additional investment. Global diesel supplies remain constrained by refinery damage in the Middle East and Russia, even as crude shipments from the Persian Gulf recover.

articles.title_orig: China expels record number of officials from CCP
articles.title_zh: China expels record number of officials from CCP
articles.content_orig:
The unprecedented number of empty seats at the fifth plenum – a symbol of expulsions – serve as a symbol for the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping
China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering , which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping.
A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.
Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history.
The confirmed expulsions included Zhang Youxia, the former second-in-command to China’s leader in the military hierarchy, and Ma Xingrui, the former party secretary for Xinjiang. Other absences were unexplained.
“More empty seats underscores the plenum’s focus on Xi’s vision of strict internal discipline,” said Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, in a post on X.
The theme for this week’s plenum was party governance. Since coming to power in 2012 Xi has focused on stamping out corruption in the party. But in recent years the campaign has intensified , taking out officials in the highest ranks of the party and the military, raising questions about if the campaign is also a tool to remove political rivals or punish disloyalty.
Xi appears to have grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a lack of discipline in the ranks of the party that wields absolute authority over the state and society in China. Earlier this year he said that the party must uproot “sick trees” and that the fight against corruption was a “never-ending journey”.
A series of purges has gutted the seven-man Central Military Commission, the ruling body of China’s People’s Liberation Army. There are now just two members left: Xi himself, and the military’s anti-graft tsar, Zhang Shengmin.
Zhang was promoted to the politburo of the CCP this week, the highest ruling body in the party. Zhang is now the only military member of the senior leadership body.
The plenum also laid the groundwork for the 21st Party congress, an event which happens every five years and is expected to next be held in the second half of 2027. Xi, who is already the longest ruler of Communist China since Mao Zedong, is expected to secure a fourth term as party leader.
The ranks of the Central Committee and the politburo will be refreshed at next year’s congress, but many analysts believe that recent purges have been so wide-ranging that there are few suitable candidates to be promoted.

articles.title_orig: The Scrapyard Search for Rare Earths
articles.title_zh: The Scrapyard Search for Rare Earths
articles.content_orig:
The technology recovers valuable rare-earth materials and converts them into reusable compounds that can be used in the production of new magnets, supporting a more circular and resilient European supply chain.
For these reasons, the International Sustainable Chemistry Collaborative Centre (ISC3) has chosen TSR Innovations as one of the finalists of the ISC3 Innovation Challenge 2026 and the start-up is featured as the ISC3 Start-up of the Month for October 2026.
A key aspect of the innovation is its use of mechanochemistry, which uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations. Unlike many conventional recycling routes, the process operates with low energy and chemical requirements and is designed to process complex waste streams that are often difficult to recycle using existing methods. By recovering valuable rare-earth materials that might otherwise be lost, TSR Innovations helps reduce resource waste and creates a secondary source of critical raw materials for future production.
From a sustainability perspective, the technology offers several advantages. According to the company, it can operate at room temperature and normal pressure. In addition, its modular design could enable deployment closer to collection points or manufacturing sites, reducing transportation needs and strengthening regional circular-economy ecosystems.
The whole success story of the ISC3 Start-up of the Month in October 2026 is currently told by the ISC3 on its website at TSR Innovations (isc3.org) .
Three questions for Tomislav Stolar (Founder and CEO of TSR Innovations)
What led you to found TSR Innovations and develop a solution in Sustainable Chemistry?
Tomislav Stolar: Mechanochemistry is a branch of chemistry that uses mechanical forces, such as those in ball milling, to drive chemical transformations. Most mechanochemical processes give high yields and run at room temperature and pressure without the need for heating or pressurization. Hence, mechanochemistry is time-, energy-, and reagent-efficient and is highly disruptive to traditional chemical manufacturing and recycling. After decades of extensive community research on mechanochemistry, I believed there was little industry application to show for it. Consequently, I took the initiative to start TSR Innovations and commercialize a mechanochemical recycling process for rare-earth magnets.
What does being chosen as ISC3 Start-up of the Month mean to you?
T. Stolar: Honestly, it means a ton. So far, we have been working in stealth on purpose, but we're now ready to move fast. ISC3 is helping us with that. We are excited about the journey ahead.
What's next up at TSR Innovations?
T. Stolar: We are ready to move from the lab to pilot scale and to significantly expand the core team. In the long term, we want to realize the first European small and modular mechanochemical long-loop recycling plant and help Europe achieve rare earth supply chain independence.

articles.title_orig: Nintendo cancels Kirby Air Riders Halloween event
articles.title_zh: Nintendo cancels Kirby Air Riders Halloween event
articles.content_orig:
Nintendo recently started up a new Halloween event for Kirby Air Riders, but it has now been cancelled.
The main menu and Paddock took on a special Halloween theme. During the event, players could earn event points to unlock Halloween-themed materials and cosmetics, including a ghost hat.
Unfortunately, players quickly noticed that the Kirby Air Riders Halloween event was very close to unplayable. You drop all boosts with one hit, which spawns all of them as items, and multiple people were getting hit per second. With so many items on screen, the game would freeze very often. The action would still be going on in the background while the screen is frozen, and during that time you’re just going straight forward and will almost always die or fall off the stage and lose all your boosts.
Nintendo recognized the issues and decided to cancel the event. The good news is that it will return at a later date – hopefully with all issues addressed.
In a statement on social media, Nintendo said:
We have confirmed an issue in the currently ongoing event “Trick or Treat!” where the screen temporarily freezes during gameplay. For this reason, we will be canceling this event.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused to our customers.
Additionally, we plan to hold the event again where this reward can be obtained. We will inform you again once the details are finalized.
For more on the game, check out our piece on the feature in Kirby Air Riders that has been forgotten .

articles.title_orig: Cheaper cars are selling considerably faster than at the beginning of the year
articles.title_zh: Cheaper cars are selling considerably faster than at the beginning of the year
articles.content_orig:
Lower-priced vehicles moved off dealer lots faster in Q3 2026 than in Q1, while tighter supply at lower price points and elevated transaction prices underscored pressure on U.S. car shoppers.
Vehicles priced from $20,000 to $29,999 spent 20% fewer days in inventory in Q3 2026 than in Q1 2026. The average time before sale fell about 18% for vehicles priced at $30,000 to $39,999 and nearly 12% for those priced at $40,000 to $49,999. These changes measure time on dealer lots, not how many vehicles were sold.
Days to turn is the average time a vehicle remains in dealer inventory before sale. Days' supply is a separate measure: It estimates how long available stock would last at the current sales pace.
Available new-vehicle inventory totaled 2.80 million units in September 2026, equal to 82 days' supply. Vehicles priced at $30,000 or less had 63 days' supply, compared with 68 days for those priced from $30,000 to $40,000 and 91 days for vehicles from $50,000 to $60,000. Vehicles under $40,000 made up about 31% of available inventory.
The average new-vehicle transaction price reached $50,562 in September 2026, up 0.7% from a year earlier and $52 below the December 2025 record. A stronger mix of lower-priced vehicles helped temper the overall increase. “Consumers don’t buy the industry average. They buy a vehicle, and prices for many of the vehicles they’re shopping are continuing to move higher,” said Erin Keating, an executive analyst at Cox Automotive.
Financing costs also remained high. Loans of at least 84 months accounted for a record 25.5% of financed new-vehicle purchases in Q3 2026, while the average monthly payment was $787, continuing the financing trends covered earlier .
Sales patterns have varied by period: Compact-car and compact-SUV sales fell more than the overall market in Q1 2026, while affordable segments later helped moderate September 2026 price growth. The faster turnover does not establish that total sales rose in the lower-priced bands.

articles.title_orig: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
articles.title_zh: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
articles.content_orig:
An Egyptian court ordered the closure of one of Egypt’s last independent news outlets Tuesday after convicting its editor in chief of operating a website without a license, a major blow to the country’s shrinking press freedom.
The publication, Mada Masr , said its editor in chief and founder, Lina Attalah, was released after paying a fine equivalent to about $53,400. She had been detained for seven hours after the verdict, with her whereabouts unknown during that time, according to the outlet.
Mada Masr is one of the few remaining news outlets in Egypt known for investigating corruption, the expanding role of the country’s powerful military and human rights violations in a country where newspapers and television stations are closely controlled by authorities. Ahead of Tuesday’s hearing, Human Rights Watch called the prosecution of Attalah an escalation of an “outrageous attack on independent media.”
Attalah’s lead lawyer, Hassan el-Azhary, said Mada Masr planned to appeal the closure order.
“Today’s decision represents a crushing blow to press freedom in Egypt and marks a dark day for independent journalism in the country,” Amnesty International said in a statement. By imposing a large fine, ordering the closure of Mada Masr and the seizure of its property, while “detaining Lina Attalah until payment is made, the Egyptian authorities are sending a clear and ruthless message: critical, independent reporting will not be tolerated.”
While completing her release paperwork, Attalah’s defense team learned that the 44-year-old journalist had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of spreading false news and operating an unlicensed website — a conviction she intends to appeal, according to Mada Masr’s Facebook page. An appeal hearing is set for Nov. 11.
During Tuesday’s session at a Cairo misdemeanor court — the first in a trial announced last week — the judge rejected all of the defense’s procedural requests and ordered its lawyers to immediately give closing arguments, said Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, a rights group, who attended the session.
When Attalah’s eight lawyers refused, the judge brought in a court-appointed lawyer none of them knew, over loud objections from the defense and from Attalah herself, Bahgat said. The judge declined to enter her rejection of the lawyer into the record, he said.
State security prosecutors summoned Attalah for questioning last week on charges of publishing false news and operating without a license, then referred her to trial on the latter charge.
Mada Masr says it first applied for a license in 2018 but never received an answer. Authorities have blocked its website inside Egypt since 2017, and the outlet says this is the sixth case brought against it or its journalists in six years.
Amnesty International and 118 other civil society groups and independent media outlets worldwide called on Egyptian authorities to stop targeting Mada Masr and grant it a license.
Khaled Elbalshy, head of the Egyptian Journalists Syndicate, the country’s press union, said in a Facebook post that the organization is standing by and supporting Attalah’s case, calling it “a wake-up call” that “runs counter to the demands” for removing press restrictions and media reform.
The case comes amid a broader crackdown on independent media in Egypt. On Tuesday, Egyptian prosecutors extended for another 15 days the pretrial detention of all six journalists of the Matsadaash investigative platform, according to a statement posted on the platform’s Facebook page.
“Their detention was extended without any new questioning, without being asked to respond to the accusations against them, and without being presented with any evidence to substantiate those allegations,” read the statement.
In late September, Matsadaash reporters were arrested on grounds of joining and financing a terrorist group and spreading false information — a generic list of charges brought against journalists and political critics in recent years.
Egypt ranks 169th among 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders’ 2026 World Press Freedom Index.

articles.title_orig: Spanish minister refuses to resign over second major train crash on his watch
articles.title_zh: Spanish minister refuses to resign over second major train crash on his watch
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here
Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has admitted “trust in high-speed rail has been broken” after Wednesday’s deadly train collision that killed at least 69 people, injured more than 100 and prompted a national debate on the safety of the country’s rail network.
Sánchez said the Spanish state was “working tirelessly” to provide information as quickly as possible to the families of the victims – who include people from at least 23 different foreign countries – adding that his government was committed to finding what had caused Spain’s second deadly train collision this year.
Two trains, one from Spain’s state-owned Renfe and the other from the private rail company Iryo, were travelling from Madrid towards the southern region of Andalucía on Wednesday when they collided just before 9am . After the Iryo train came to a halt, the other slammed into its rear , knocking several carriages off the track near Urda in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha.
The crash came nine months after 46 people were killed and dozens injured when two trains – one from Renfe and one from Iryo – collided on the same line near the town of Adamuz in Andalucía.
“ It’s unacceptable for a country like Spain – which has such a powerful high-speed rail system – to experience two accidents of this nature and magnitude within a single year,” the prime minister said on Friday.
“Therefore, our task isn’t merely to investigate the causes of what occurred, but also to provide solutions to further strengthen our nation’s high-speed rail system.
Public trust in the high-speed system has been broken ; the government’s responsibility goes beyond diagnosing the causes – it must also offer solutions to ensure that a tragedy of this scale doesn’t happen again.”
Shortly after Sánchez spoke, Spain’s transport minister, Óscar Puente – who is under growing pressure to resign – gave a press conference in which he dismissed calls to step down, promising instead to focus on “providing the Spanish people with solutions” to restore trust.
“My duty now isn’t to talk about whether or not I carry on with my job; it’s to solve the problems, clarify what happened and offer clear explanations,” he said. “ The most important thing I can do is offer solutions as best I can. If the investigation shows there were failures of organisation or control, we will act accordingly. And if individuals are found to be responsible, action will be taken.”
Puente once again suggested that responsibility for Wednesday’s crash appeared to lie within the Madrid control centre of Spain’s state infrastructure operator, Adif. He said that in the run-up to the crash, the LZB signalling system – which automatically halts a train if the line ahead is occupied – had gone down, but stressed that such incidents were not at all uncommon. Once the system was down, he said, control and decision-making powers ultimately reverted to humans, as was the case in other transport sectors.
And, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today .

The incumbent Iliana Yotova , former vice-president to Bulgaria’s former president and current prime minister Rumen Radev , faces pro-European opposition candidate, Andrey Gyurov.
The two candidates will pit contrasting political visions against each other in a highly polarised contest on Sunday, AP noted.
Contrary to pre-election expectations by observers for a double-digit difference in favour of Yotova, her opponent showed a surprisingly strong performance coming just 2.8 percentage points behind her and leaving all options open for the runoff.

The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta has announced it is closing, citing pressure from authorities who recently searched the home of its senior editor and earlier this year detained one of its journalists.
“Novaya Gazeta is ceasing to exist,” the editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, said in a video statement published on YouTube on Friday. “The Russian authorities – the Russian special services – have forced the editorial team to end its work.”
Russia has introduced near-Soviet levels of censorship since sending troops to Ukraine, pushing the vast majority of independent journalists into exile. Novaya Gazeta, a bastion of independent journalism in Russia, is classed by Moscow as a “foreign agent”, a label used to stifle dissent.
Sokolov said: “ Novaya Gazeta has been killed … On 9 November we will turn off the lights in our home, where we have lived for 30 years. We will shut down the servers and leave.”
This month Sokolov was taken in for questioning and Russian authorities searched his home over a criminal case involving one of his colleagues, Oleg Roldugin, who was arrested in April.
Russia has intensified its crackdown on independent news outlets since its offensive on Ukraine in February 2022. Novaya Gazeta cut down production inside Russia after the offensive began. Authorities revoked its media licence the same year.
The paper’s then editor-in-chief, Dmitry Muratov, jointly won the Nobel peace prize in 2021 for his “efforts to safeguard freedom of expression” at the helm of the paper.

articles.title_orig: Review: Predator Atlas 8: Is Arc G3 Extreme a Game-Changer for PC Handhelds?
articles.title_zh: Review: Predator Atlas 8: Is Arc G3 Extreme a Game-Changer for PC Handhelds?
articles.content_orig:
Acer's $1300 / £1300 Predator Atlas 8 is here, one of a handful of new PC handhelds to launch this year despite crippling price rises to components like RAM and SSDs. The special sauce here is Intel's first handheld-specific chipset, the Arc G3 Extreme. Does the new hardware move the needle compared to existing AMD Z2 Extreme handhelds like the ROG Xbox Ally X20 ? And how does Acer's handheld compare to better-known rivals like Valve, Asus and MSI in terms of design?
Before we get into the performance testing, it's worth quickly running through the design of Atlas 8. It's a chunky, handsome device in a pleasant dark grey chassis, and I like the colours chosen for the face buttons. However, it does feel a step behind rivals like the Xbox Ally X when it comes ergonomics, with quite geometrically basic grips and a robust 810g weight - significantly heavier than a 640g Steam Deck or 540g Switch 2.
The sticks and triggers use modern TMR sensors, which is great for longevity and precision, but the circular d-pad leaves a little to be desired and the buzzy, off-putting vibration makes it feel like you're holding a horrendous metallic wasp - some distance away from the more detailed and restrained Microsoft-derived Xbox Ally devices when it comes to vibration.
The eight-inch 1920x1200 120Hz VRR screen is thankfully a lot more competitive. It's no OLED when it comes to contrast and colour reproduction, but it gets bright enough for outdoor use, provides wide viewing angles and doesn't exhibit any distracting ghosting or other artefacts, so fast motion looks good. Overall, it's a better offering than the Switch 2's LCD, but a step behind the Steam Deck OLED - and with the powerful Arc G3 Extreme chipset on board, the handheld has the genuine capability of reaching high frame-rate territory for a change. The prominent speakers flanking the bottom of the screen are also amongst the loudest I've ever heard on a handheld, and I spent most of my time with the volume at around 10 percent as a result.
When it comes to performance, Intel's Arc G3 Extreme is a massive step beyond the AMD Z2 Extreme chipset that powers the Xbox Ally X.
The Atlas 8 was able to outperform the Xbox Ally X by around 50 to 70 percent at matched settings at a rated TDP of 35W, albeit with the Xbox Ally X using FSR 4 - which carries a small performance penalty, often around 5 percent. Generally speaking, this brought average sub-60fps games on the Xbox Ally X into the 80s and 90s, allowing extra headroom for increasing settings or simply a more responsive experience that takes better advantage of the 120Hz display.
The Atlas 8 offers four options - a 25W quiet mode, 30W balanced mode and 35W turbo mode, while a manual setting allows you to bump up the total to 40W - though its jargon-filled warning ("Changing PL1/PL2 may cause system instability") needs rewriting in plain English.
I only had the Atlas 8 for around four days of testing, so I focused my attention on five games with built-in benchmarks at 35W on both machines: Civilization 7 (CPU and GPU), F1 25: 2026 Season Edition, Forza Horizon 6, Returnal and Red Dead Redemption 2. The full results, including game settings, are shown below.
(1080p XeSS/FSR Auto, High)
F1 25: 2026 Season Edition
(1080p XeSS/FSR Quality, High)
(1080p XeSS/FSR Quality, Low)
(1080p FSR Balanced, Prefer perf.)
While the Atlas 8 performs incredibly well, even the brief testing experience I had was held back by a litany of bugs and poor design decisions in Windows 11. Despite improvements to the Xbox launcher and better usability for gamepad controls, the initial setup experience is torturously long and asks many irrelevant questions for a gaming handheld; driver and software updates are spread amongst nearly half a dozen different places; and at several points applications crashed or simply stopped working, necessitating a restart. I'm hesitant to blame Acer for any of these problems, as I experienced many similar issues on the Xbox Ally X, which has been on the market for considerably longer.
To take just one example, I wanted to install GPU driver updates before testing. New drivers weren't available via Windows Update, nor were they offered in the Intel Arc Control app. I eventually used Edge to visit the Intel Driver and Support Assistant page, which required a separate download and install. Once this was finished, the page had a generic error message, which I needed to fix by clicking on the lock icon next to the URL in Edge, setting the "apps on device" setting to enabled, and reloading the page. This was frustrating enough as a long-time user of Windows and Windows handhelds, so I can't imagine what it would be like for a relative newcomer. On SteamOS, by contrast, this would have been sorted with a simple trip to the Settings menu to install the latest updates.
Other issues I experienced in just a few days with the device included some Steam games missing from the Xbox launcher, Windows Firewall messages still popping up in the year of our lord 2026, the handheld's lights and fans remaining on while the screen and buttons stop working, games missing from the alt-tab and Xbox switcher menus while running, Explorer not responding to touch inputs, and taking nearly two hours to reset Windows 11 back to stock after testing while I waited, already long overdue in bed.
As Rich says in the X20 review : "This didn't feel like any kind of console experience - because too much of standard Windows intrudes and in that sense, it still feels off-putting."
It's much the same on the Atlas 8, and that's a shame. Perhaps the likes of SteamOS, Bazzite and other handheld-focused Linux distributions could give these handhelds a better user experience, but expect driver compatibility to be an issue at least in the short to medium term. For now, the expectation is that these are Windows 11 devices, and that means accepting some level of usability compromises versus Steam Deck or Switch 2.
Despite the rough edges that persist in Windows, the $1300 / £1300 Atlas 8 is still a great handheld that is well worth considering. The surfeit of performance available here brings a new generation of games into handheld playability, even if Intel's XeSS has fallen a little behind the latest generations of DLSS and FSR. The design work here is also solid, with some ergonomic improvements and weight saving to find in later iterations, but fundamentally there's nothing here that prevents the Atlas 8 from becoming your primary gaming device on the go.
The new Acer handheld is about to be released in the US - Best Buy shows a November 2nd release date - and I'm fascinated to read more reviews from critics and users alike once the handheld is available for a wider audience. For example, I'd be interested to see more in-depth testing of performance and battery life when gaming in quiet mode. As always, individual reviews are necessarily limited in scope, so I encourage you to read widely to get a balanced view.

articles.title_orig: 3 Arrested in Connection With Deadly Blast in Central Athens
articles.title_zh: 3 Arrested in Connection With Deadly Blast in Central Athens
articles.content_orig:
Three men accused of damaging a natural gas pipeline while attempting to steal copper face serious charges over last month’s explosion in Athens’ Plaka district that killed six people.
The suspects, two Greeks and an Albanian national, have been charged with arson and causing an explosion, both allegedly committed intentionally and jointly, resulting in deaths. They also face multiple counts of homicide with possible intent and causing dangerous bodily harm.
Investigators believe the men tampered with copper pipes connected to the gas installation in a building on Lysikratous Street, causing a leak that led to the September 25 blast. Security camera footage allegedly shows the three entering the building’s ground-floor stairwell several hours before the explosion.
Authorities suspect the men were attempting to remove copper pipes connected to the gas supply meter. In doing so, they may have damaged an active gas line, allowing gas to leak and accumulate inside the building.
Investigators are also examining how the gas ignited. One possibility under consideration is that an elderly woman who lived with her husband on the second floor switched on an electrical light, generating a spark that ignited the accumulated gas.
The explosion killed six people: the elderly couple and two couples of tourists staying in a short-term rental on the building’s first floor.
The suspects are reportedly known to authorities and are also being investigated over alleged illegal activities elsewhere in the area on the day of the explosion. Their movements before the blast remain under scrutiny.
The investigation, led by the Fire Service’s Arson Crimes Division, has involved the analysis of security camera footage, communications data and evidence recovered from the scene, as well as examinations by specialist experts. The explosion caused the collapse of the two-storey building.

Motorola first showed off the Signature 27 during Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit back in September , but it's been holding back the full specs and pricing ever since. Yesterday, its Indian website said the phone is "coming this November" , and now the company has narrowed that down to an exact date: November 5.
Here's what we already know. The Signature 27 is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, cooled by an ArcticMesh system with a vapor chamber that's 40% larger than the previous generation's.
There's a 50MP Sony Lytia 910 main camera with OIS and a 200MP periscope telephoto, plus Audio by Bang & Olufsen . The rest of the camera setup still hasn't been detailed, and there do seem to be a lot of cameras in its gigantic camera bump, so we're definitely intrigued, to say the least. Price-wise, a recent retailer listing from Europe confirms that this won't be an affordable device.

articles.title_orig: Treasury Department announces new Series I bond rate of 5.51% for the next six months
articles.title_zh: Treasury Department announces new Series I bond rate of 5.51% for the next six months
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
T-Mobile (TMUS) declared a $1.17 quarterly dividend representing a 14.7% raise, but the stock has fallen 26% year to date, which has artificially inflated today's 3.2% yield.
I bonds pay 4.26% with inflation protection and state-tax exemption but limit purchases to $10,000 per year and lock up cash for 12 months.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and T-Mobile didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat TMUS. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
Series I savings bonds carry a 4.26% composite rate on bonds issued from May 1, 2026 through October 31, 2026. That window closes this week, and a new rate applies to bonds issued starting November 1, 2026. On the stock side, T-Mobile ( NASDAQ:TMUS ) traded at $146.32 in premarket trading on October 28, 2026. Against its annualized forward dividend of $4.68 per share, that works out to an indicated yield of about 3.2%. Neither number is a guaranteed return, and they differ in more ways than the rate.
An I bond is a savings bond sold directly by the U.S. Treasury. Its rate has two parts. The first is a fixed rate , currently 0.9%. It stays with the bond for its full life. The second is a semiannual inflation rate , currently 1.67%. It tracks inflation and resets every six months. Treasury combines the two with its own formula to produce the composite rate. The inflation component is never locked. It can fall as easily as it can rise, and each bond's rate changes every six months from its issue date.
The rules are strict, and they matter to anyone who may need the cash:

Why Didn't TMUS Make The Top 10 List?

Purchase cap: electronic purchases are limited to $10,000 per person per year.
Lockup: you cannot cash the bond for the first 12 months.
Early-redemption penalty: cash it before five years and you give up the last three months of interest.
Maturity: the bond earns interest for 30 years, then ends. Your original investment plus all accrued interest is paid to you at redemption.
Interest is added to the bond's value instead of being paid out as cash. Anyone who needs a quarterly check must redeem the bond to get it.
Start with whether the payment holds up. T-Mobile's dividend has grown fast. It paid $0.65 per share per quarter through 2024, $0.88 in 2025, and $1.02 starting in late 2025. On September 24, 2026, the board declared a $1.17 per share dividend, a 14.7% increase. It goes ex-dividend on November 25, 2026, and pays on December 10, 2026.
Cash flow covers it well. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance to between $18.4 billion and $18.8 billion, with cash capex of about $10 billion. Second-quarter free cash flow was $4.797 billion. The board's 2026 shareholder return authorization of up to $18.2 billion covers both buybacks and dividends, and buybacks are the flexible piece. Since the program began in Q3 2022, T-Mobile has returned $44.2 billion through buybacks and $10.4 billion through dividends.
Those strains are real, though. Total debt excluding tower obligations stood at $86.9 billion as of Q2 2026. Postpaid churn rose to 0.99%, and costs from the UScellular merger and the retail overhaul are still running through results. The CFO said the company is maintaining a capital budget for spectrum auctions in 2027 and 2028, which will compete with cash for shareholder returns.
Investors have noticed. The stock is down 26.35% year-to-date and 31.91% over the past year. Telecom shares also slid after reports that SpaceX had held cell tower talks for Starlink Mobile (Forbes). Much of today's yield comes from that falling price, not from a fatter payout.
Here is the core tradeoff. A Treasury-backed I bond cannot have its payment cut by a board, and its redemption value never falls. It also cannot grow beyond what the fixed rate and the inflation formula deliver. A T-Mobile dividend can grow, as it has every year since it started, and it still has room to grow. It can also be cut, and the shares behind it can lose value. The stock's 11.55% drop over the past month shows how quickly that can happen.
I bonds carry risks of their own. The government guarantee covers your principal and accrued interest. It does not cover your purchasing power beyond what the formula captures, and it does not let you buy more than the annual cap. The biggest risk is reinvestment risk : if inflation cools, the variable component resets lower, and the composite rate falls with it, while the 0.9% fixed portion stays put. Money is also tied up for a year, and you give up interest if you redeem early.
The federal government taxes I bond interest as ordinary income. It is exempt from state and local taxes. Cash-method taxpayers can also defer the federal tax until the earlier of the year you cash or dispose of the bonds or the year in which they mature. That lets a retiree choose the year the income shows up, ideally a low-income year. Interest may also be excluded under the Education Savings Bond Program if you redeem bonds in the same year you pay qualified higher education expenses, such as a grandchild's tuition, subject to that program's rules.
T-Mobile's dividends count as qualified dividends if you meet the holding-period test. Federal law treats qualified dividend income as net capital gain under 26 U.S.C. § 1(h)(11), so it is taxed at the preferential rates for long-held assets, which are usually lower than ordinary income rates. Dividends are taxable at the state level, and you owe tax in the year you receive them, with no option to defer. The I bond's state exemption helps where state taxes are high. In a no-income-tax state, the lower federal rate on dividends may count for more.
I bonds suit retirees who want inflation-linked savings that can never lose value, who can leave the money alone for at least a year (ideally five), and who live in a high-tax state or want to choose when interest becomes taxable. T-Mobile's dividend fits income investors who want quarterly cash today and a payout with a record of growth, and who can ride out share-price declines like this year's. Before relying on that payout, they should be comfortable with the company's debt load and its spectrum spending plans. articles.title_orig: Goodwill Seemingly Has No Clue It’s Selling a Previously Unknown Leica Prototype Lens
articles.title_zh: Goodwill Seemingly Has No Clue It’s Selling a Previously Unknown Leica Prototype Lens
articles.content_orig:
An exceedingly rare Leica prototype lens is up for auction right now. No, it’s not at Leitz Photographica or Wetzlar Camera Auctions. It’s at Goodwill .
Per Lenstag’s founder, Trevor Sehrer, this lens appears to be a previously unknown second copy of a very rare prototype lens that most recently sold for nearly $50,000.
In 2021, PetaPixel reported on what was then believed to be a one-of-a-kind prototype: the Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2. Leica Store Lisse was selling the 26-pound behemoth lens for $47,200. This same lens had been listed on eBay four years prior for $24,000, as Leica Rumors wrote in January 2018.
A Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 prototype lens, which looks identical to the one sold in 2021 except for its C530-0004 model number rather than the C530-0007 one seen five years ago, is somehow at Goodwill of the Great Plains in Sioux Falls, South Dakota right now.
It’s being sold in “as is” condition. It seems Goodwill doesn’t fully appreciate what it has on its hands, listing it like a regular lens instead of the treasure it is.
”We do our best to describe items completely and accurately, but we are not experts,” Goodwill warns, adding that prospective bidders should look very carefully at the included photos, as they are effectively serving as the product’s description.
Even if the Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 lens available right now at Goodwill is not in great condition — although it does look good — it remains an exceptionally collectible piece of photographic history.
People have stumbled upon incredible Leica gear in unusual places before. Last year, Ontario photographer Brandon Simpson found a $2,000 Leica at a thrift store for $10 . A teenager in 2021 found an entire Leica M kit for $15 at a church sale. A few years before that, a college student grabbed a Leica M5 at a thrift store for just $5.
At the time of writing, Goodwill’s Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 prototype lens is $3,008 after seven bids . While it’s much pricier than the thrift store finds above, it may still sell for what amounts to a steal. The bidding ends at 9:50 PM ET (6:50 PM PT) today, October 30. Good luck.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu's bloc falls short as longtime allies reportedly weigh move that could end his rule
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu's bloc falls short as longtime allies reportedly weigh move that could end his rule
articles.content_orig:
With final election results leaving both major blocs short of a majority, Fox News Digital reporter Efrat Lachter reports from Israel on the negotiations that could determine the country's next government.
Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors.
The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee , gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position.
Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results .
ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW
Posters of former Israeli Chief of General Staff and Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot, right, and Prime Minister and Likud Party leader Benjamin Netanyahu are seen as election campaigns intensify two days before the vote as campaign posters of candidates are displayed on billboards and buildings across the streets ahead of the Knesset elections scheduled for October 27, in Tel Aviv, Israel, on October 25, 2026. (Nir Keidar/Anadolu via Getty Images)
But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals.
A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation.
The source said opposition leaders are approaching coalition negotiations with patience and experience rather than treating the inconclusive results as a defeat, arguing that the next government could depend on their ability to forge partnerships that previously seemed unlikely.
FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER
An ultra-Orthodox Jewish man holds his ballot as he votes in the parliamentary election at a polling station in Jerusalem on January 22, 2013. Israelis voted on Tuesday in an election widely expected to win Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a third term in office, pushing the Jewish State further to the right, away from peace with Palestinians and towards a showdown with Iran. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
In a potentially significant development Friday, Israeli journalist Yishai Cohen of Kikar HaShabbat reported that Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading ultra-Orthodox religious authority, had instructed lawmakers from Degel HaTorah, part of United Torah Judaism, to open discussions with the opposition.
According to the report, the objective is to reach an arrangement protecting the status of yeshiva students amid the longstanding dispute over mandatory military service.
Channel 12 reported that figures within the ultra-Orthodox party were considering allowing an Eisenkot-led minority government to survive through outside parliamentary support, potentially breaking with Netanyahu.
"Our votes are not in Netanyahu's pocket," party figures told Channel 12, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language report.
However, the office of United Torah Judaism Chairman Yaakov Asher denied that any instruction to begin negotiations had been issued.
Such an arrangement would represent a significant shift from the party's longstanding alliance with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's pledge to expand military conscription among ultra-Orthodox men remains a major obstacle, although Channel 12 reported that party figures were willing to consider a compromise on the issue.
The source familiar with opposition discussions told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot's camp had been preparing for the possibility of cooperation with ultra-Orthodox parties well before the election, suggesting that some of the options now being discussed had already been under consideration behind the scenes.
According to the source, such an arrangement could require compromises over military service and potentially outside parliamentary support from Arab lawmakers, bringing together political factions whose positions appeared irreconcilable during the campaign.
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
People gather near a pre-election campaign banner featuring leaders of the Joint List, ahead of Israel's national election, in Nazareth, Israel, on October 10, 2026. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)
Another possibility rests with the Arab parties, which nearly doubled their parliamentary representation from 10 to 19 seats following a surge in turnout.
But the prospects of an Arab-backed government have drawn conflicting assessments.
Channel 12 reported Thursday that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas had expressed deep skepticism about the possibility of establishing an Eisenkot-led minority government supported by Arab lawmakers.
Israeli political commentator Amit Segal also argued that the available options had narrowed considerably, identifying a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government or another election as the two principal remaining possibilities.
Mohammed Majadla, head of the news division at Radio Nas and a Channel 12 political commentator, offered a different assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital, arguing that both Ra'am and the Joint List were prepared to use their parliamentary influence to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power.
"The two Arab lists agree on two things," Majadla said in the Hebrew-language interview. "First, they are prepared to do everything within the political process to ensure Netanyahu does not return to power."
According to Majadla, that could include joining a coalition, providing outside parliamentary support or abstaining from key votes.
He said their second shared priority was avoiding another election, which Arab political leaders fear could reverse their gains.
"The ball is now in Eisenkot's court, not in the Arab parties' court," Majadla said. "As far as the Arab parties are concerned, I can tell you they are truly prepared to do everything to make this happen."
Majadla suggested that public declarations should not necessarily be treated as final positions, particularly as parties seek leverage during coalition negotiations.
The difficulties extend beyond the Arab parties. Eisenkot's potential partners include politicians who strongly oppose cooperation with ultra-Orthodox factions, while several opposition leaders campaigned against relying on Arab lawmakers to govern.
NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING
A road sign stands in front of a large billboard featuring Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, of the Likud Party and former military chief and leader of the centrist Yashar Party, Gadi Eisenkot, in Ramat Gan on October 20, 2026. Israel heads to the polls on October 27 in its first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack, in what is seen as a referendum on the prime minister. (Jack Guez / AFP via Getty Images)
A national unity government involving Likud and Yashar would offer a more straightforward mathematical route to a majority, but would require Eisenkot to reconsider his campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government.

articles.title_orig: John Romero confirms his axed Xbox game has a new publisher and he’s rehired some staff
articles.title_zh: John Romero confirms his axed Xbox game has a new publisher and he’s rehired some staff
articles.content_orig:
Translated with AI from the Russian original .
Romero Games managed to save the project.
id Software co-founder and Doom and Quake co-creator John Romero announced that his studio Romero Games has found a new publisher for its unannounced shooter. In addition, some of the employees who previously left the team after losing funding from Microsoft have returned to work on the project.
In the summer of 2026, Romero Games confirmed that it had lost development funding for the game after Microsoft backed out of the publishing agreement. This occurred amid large-scale layoffs within the corporation. As a result, the studio had to significantly downsize: out of the original 110 employees, only five remained.
Now, speaking to VGC journalists at Gamescom Asia, Romero shared that he managed to reach an agreement with a new publisher. Its name, partnership terms, and official announcement date have not yet been disclosed.
According to the developer, the studio has already brought ten people back to the team, including heads of various departments. Around 15–16 employees are currently working at Romero Games. There are no plans to expand the staff in the near future: the project has been redesigned to match the capabilities of a small team.
Romero emphasized that it will no longer be possible to finish the original version of the game. It was conceived with a 110-person team in mind, so the studio essentially had to create a new project while preserving a significant portion of the previously developed materials.
Specifically, the developers are using assets and progress from the previous version: characters, artwork, weapons, graphical assets, and code. According to Romero, this gave them a major head start in development.
The developer also noted that he prefers working with smaller teams. This format allows him to personally engage in the day-to-day game development, make decisions, work directly in Unreal Editor, and handle design instead of spending most of his time in meetings.
Romero also commented separately on the collaboration with the new publisher. According to him, they have made no creative demands and fully trust the studio on development matters.
